title.zh: 卷一百六十六 志第一百十九 職官六
title.raw: 卷一百六十六 志第一百十九 職官六 Volume 166 Treatises 119: Offical Posts 6

sentences.zh: 職官六

translations.literal: Official Posts 6
translations.idiomatic: Official Posts, Part Six

sentences.zh: ○殿前司侍衛親軍環衛官皇城司三衛官客省引進四方館東西上閣門帶禦器械人內內侍省內侍省開封府臨安府河南應天府次府節度使承宣觀察防禦等使

translations.literal: ○ Bureau of the Palace Command; Imperial Guard; Palace Guard ranks; Imperial City Bureau; Three Guards offices; Reception Bureau; Introduction Bureau; Four Directions Hostel; Eastern and Western Upper Gate offices; bearers of imperial arms; Inner Palace; Inner Palace Service; Kaifeng Prefecture; Lin'an Prefecture; Henan, Yingtian, and secondary prefectures; military commissioners; commissioners of promotion, observation, and defense, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Bureau of the Palace Command; Imperial Guard; Palace Guard ranks; Imperial City Bureau; Three Guards offices; Reception Bureau; Introduction Bureau; Four Directions Hostel; Eastern and Western Upper Gate offices; bearers of imperial arms; Inner Palace; Inner Palace Service; Kaifeng Prefecture; Lin'an Prefecture; Henan, Yingtian, and secondary prefectures; military commissioners; and commissioners of promotion, observation, defense, and the like.

sentences.zh: 【殿前司】都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候各一人。

translations.literal: Bureau of the Palace Command: one commander-in-chief, one vice commander-in-chief, and one chief inspector each.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of the Palace Command: there was one commander-in-chief, one vice commander-in-chief, and one chief inspector.

sentences.zh: 掌殿前諸班直及步騎諸指揮之名籍，凡統製、訓練、番衛、戍守、遷補、賞罰，皆總其政令。

translations.literal: They managed the registers of all palace detachments and direct units and of all cavalry and infantry commands, and oversaw all policies for command, training, rotation of guard duty, garrison service, promotion and transfer, and rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the registers of all palace detachments and direct units and of all cavalry and infantry commands, and oversaw every matter of command, training, guard rotation, garrison duty, promotion and transfer, and rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 而有都點檢、副都點檢之名，在都指揮之上，後不復置，入則侍衛殿陛，出則扈從乘輿，大禮則提點編排，整肅禁衛鹵簿儀仗，掌宿衛之事，都指揮使以節度使為之。

translations.literal: There were also titles of chief inspector and vice chief inspector, ranking above the commander-in-chief; these were later abolished. When within the palace they attended upon the throne hall; when abroad they escorted the imperial carriage. On great ceremonies they supervised arrangement and marshaled the forbidden guard, insignia, and ceremonial regalia, and managed night-watch duties. The commander-in-chief was filled by a military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: There had also been the posts of chief inspector and vice chief inspector, ranking above the commander-in-chief, but these were later abolished. Within the palace they attended the throne hall; abroad they escorted the imperial carriage. On state ceremonies they supervised arrangements and kept the forbidden guard, insignia, and ceremonial regalia in order, and they managed palace night-watch duty. The commander-in-chief was normally a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 而副都指揮使、都虞候以刺史以上充。

translations.literal: The vice commander-in-chief and chief inspector were filled by officials of prefectural commissioner rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The vice commander-in-chief and chief inspector were drawn from officials of prefectural commissioner rank or higher.

sentences.zh: 資序淺則主管本司公事，馬步軍亦如之。

translations.literal: If seniority was shallow, one supervised the routine business of the bureau; the cavalry and infantry commands followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: When seniority was relatively low, an officer would supervise the bureau's routine business; the cavalry and infantry commands followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 備則通治，闕則互攝。

translations.literal: When all posts were filled, they governed jointly; when one was vacant, they acted for one another.
translations.idiomatic: When all posts were filled they governed jointly; when one was vacant they covered for one another.

sentences.zh: 凡軍事皆行以法，而治其獄訟。

translations.literal: All military matters were carried out according to law, and they adjudicated lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: All military affairs were handled according to law, and they also adjudicated lawsuits within the command.

sentences.zh: 若情不中法，則稟奏聽旨。

translations.literal: If the circumstances did not fit the law, they reported upward and awaited imperial instruction.
translations.idiomatic: If the facts did not fit the statute, they reported upward and awaited the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 騎軍有殿前指揮使、內殿直、散員、散指揮、散都頭、散祗候、金槍班、東西班、散直、鈞容直及捧日以下諸軍指揮，步軍有禦龍直、骨朵子直、弓箭直、弩直及天武以下諸軍指揮。

translations.literal: The cavalry had the Palace Command detachment, Inner Hall Direct, scattered personnel, scattered commanders, scattered company heads, scattered attendants, Golden Spear Company, Eastern and Western Classes, scattered direct service, Tuned Containment Direct, and all army commands from Sun-bearer downward; the infantry had Imperial Dragon Direct, Mace Direct, Bow Direct, Crossbow Direct, and all army commands from Heaven's Martial downward.
translations.idiomatic: Among the cavalry were the Palace Command detachment, Inner Hall Direct, scattered personnel, scattered commanders, scattered company heads, scattered attendants, the Golden Spear Company, the Eastern and Western Classes, scattered direct service, Tuned Containment Direct, and all commands from Sun-bearer downward; among the infantry were Imperial Dragon Direct, Mace Direct, Bow Direct, Crossbow Direct, and all commands from Heaven's Martial downward.

sentences.zh: 諸班有都都虞候指揮使、都軍使、都知、副都知、押班。

translations.literal: Each detachment had chief-of-chiefs inspector-commander, army commander, chief steward, vice chief steward, and escort shift leader.
translations.idiomatic: Each detachment had its chief-of-chiefs inspector-commander, army commander, chief steward, vice chief steward, and escort shift leader.

sentences.zh: 禦龍諸直，有四直都虞候，本直各有虞候、指揮使、副指揮使、都頭、副都頭、十將、將虞候。

translations.literal: The Imperial Dragon direct units had a chief inspector over the four direct units; each direct unit had its own inspector, commander, vice commander, company head, vice company head, squad leader of ten, and officer-inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Dragon direct units had a chief inspector over all four direct units; each direct unit in turn had its inspector, commander, vice commander, company head, vice company head, squad leader of ten, and officer-inspector.

sentences.zh: 騎軍、步軍，有捧日、天武左右四廂都指揮使，捧日、天武左右廂各有都指揮使。

translations.literal: Cavalry and infantry each had commanders-in-chief over the left and right four wings of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial; each left and right wing of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial had its own commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry and infantry each had commanders-in-chief over the left and right four wings of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial, and each wing of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial had its own commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 每軍有都指揮使、都虞候，每指揮有指揮使、副指揮使，每都有軍使、副兵馬使、十將、將虞候、承局、押官，各以其職隸於殿前司。

translations.literal: Each army had a commander-in-chief and chief inspector; each command had a commander and vice commander; each company had an army officer, vice horse-and-arms officer, squad leader of ten, officer-inspector, clerk, and escort officer—all subordinate to the Bureau of the Palace Command according to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had a commander-in-chief and chief inspector; each command had a commander and vice commander; each company had an army officer, vice horse-and-arms officer, squad leader of ten, officer-inspector, clerk, and escort officer, all subordinate to the Bureau of the Palace Command according to their duties.

sentences.zh: 元祐七年，簽書樞密院王岩叟言：「祖宗以來，三帥不曾闕兩人，若殿帥闕，難於從下超補，姚麟係殿前都虞候，合升作步軍副都指揮使。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanyou, Wang Yansou, who signed documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs, said: "Since the founding ancestors, the three commanders have never been short two at once. If the palace commander is vacant, it is hard to promote someone from below out of turn. Yao Lin is chief inspector of the Palace Command and ought to be promoted to vice commander-in-chief of the Infantry Command."
translations.idiomatic: In 1092, Wang Yansou, signing secretary at the Bureau of Military Affairs, said: "Since the founding ancestors, the Three Commands have never been short two commanders at once. When the palace commander is vacant, it is difficult to promote someone from the lower ranks out of turn. Yao Lin is chief inspector of the Palace Command and should be promoted to vice commander-in-chief of the Infantry Command."

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，詔：「殿前指揮使金槍弩手班、龍旗直所減人額及排定班分，並依元豐詔旨。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, an edict said: "The reduced quotas and fixed shift assignments of the Palace Command detachment, Golden Spear crossbowmen company, and Dragon Banner Direct shall all follow the Yuanfeng edict."
translations.idiomatic: In 1096, an edict ordered: "The reduced quotas and fixed shift assignments of the Palace Command detachment, Golden Spear crossbowmen company, and Dragon Banner Direct shall all follow the Yuanfeng edict."

sentences.zh: 政和四年，詔：「殿前都指揮使在節度使之上，殿前副都指揮使在正任承宣使之上，殿前都虞候在正任防禦使之上。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe, an edict said: "The palace commander-in-chief ranks above a military commissioner; the palace vice commander-in-chief ranks above a regular commissioner of promotion; the palace chief inspector ranks above a regular commissioner of defense."
translations.idiomatic: In 1114, an edict declared: "The palace commander-in-chief ranks above a military commissioner; the palace vice commander-in-chief ranks above a regular commissioner of promotion; and the palace chief inspector ranks above a regular commissioner of defense."

sentences.zh: 渡江後，都指揮間虛不除，則以主管殿前司一員任其事。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, when the post of commander-in-chief was often left vacant and unfilled, one officer as supervisor of the Bureau of the Palace Command was assigned to handle its duties.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed the Yangzi, when the commander-in-chief was often left vacant, a single officer supervising the Bureau of the Palace Command was assigned to handle its affairs.

sentences.zh: 其屬有幹辦公事、主管禁衛二員，淮備差遣、淮備差使、點檢醫藥飯食各一員，書寫機宜文字一員。

translations.literal: Its subordinates included two handlers of routine business and two supervisors of forbidden guards; one officer each for reserve dispatch, reserve assignment, and inspection of medicine and food; and one clerk for confidential documents.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff included two handlers of routine business and two supervisors of the forbidden guard; one officer each for reserve dispatch, reserve assignment, and inspection of medicine and food; and one clerk for confidential documents.

sentences.zh: 本司掌諸班直禁旅扈衛之事，捧日、天武四廂隸焉。

translations.literal: This bureau managed all detachments, direct units, forbidden troops, and escort duties; the four wings of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: This bureau managed all detachments, direct units, forbidden troops, and escort duties, and the four wings of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial were subordinate to it.

sentences.zh: 訓齊其眾，振飭其藝，通輪內宿，並宿衛親兵並聽節制。

translations.literal: It trained and aligned the ranks, sharpened their skills, rotated inner palace night duty, and all palace-guard direct troops obeyed its command.
translations.idiomatic: It trained and aligned the ranks, sharpened their skills, rotated inner-palace night duty, and all palace-guard direct troops were subject to its command.

sentences.zh: 其下有統製、統領、將佐等分任其事。

translations.literal: Below it were controllers, leaders, and adjutants who divided the duties.
translations.idiomatic: Below it were controllers, leaders, and adjutants who divided the work among themselves.

sentences.zh: 凡諸軍班直功賞、轉補，行門拍試、換官，閱實排連以詔於上；

translations.literal: For all army detachments and direct units, merit rewards and transfers, gate-examination trials and rank changes, and verified roster arrangements were reported upward by edict;
translations.idiomatic: For all army detachments and direct units, it handled merit rewards and transfers, gate-examination trials and rank changes, and verified roster arrangements, reporting these upward by edict;

sentences.zh: 諸殿侍差使年滿出職，祗應參班，核其名籍；

translations.literal: when palace service envoys completed their term and left office, it received their attendance in formation and checked their registers;
translations.idiomatic: when palace service envoys completed their terms and left office, it received their attendance in formation and checked their registers;

sentences.zh: 以時教閱，則謹鞍馬、軍器、衣甲之出入；

translations.literal: at scheduled drill and review it strictly controlled the issue and return of saddles, horses, weapons, and armor;
translations.idiomatic: at scheduled drill and review it strictly controlled the issue and return of saddles, horses, weapons, and armor;

sentences.zh: 軍兵有獄訟，則以法鞫治。

translations.literal: when soldiers had lawsuits, it tried them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: and when soldiers were involved in lawsuits, it tried them according to law.

sentences.zh: 初，渡江草創，三衙之制未備，稍稍招集，填置三帥。

translations.literal: At first, in the founding period after crossing the Yangzi, the system of the Three Commands was not complete; troops were gradually recruited and the three commanders were filled in.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the founding period after the court crossed the Yangzi, the system of the Three Commands was incomplete; troops were gradually recruited and the three commanders were filled in.

sentences.zh: 資淺才，各有主管某司公事之稱。

translations.literal: Those of shallow seniority each bore the title of supervising routine business of a given bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of shallow seniority each held the title of supervising routine business of a given bureau.

sentences.zh: 又別置御營司，擢王淵為都統製。

translations.literal: An Imperial Camp Bureau was also separately established, and Wang Yuan was promoted to chief controller.
translations.idiomatic: An Imperial Camp Bureau was also established separately, and Wang Yuan was promoted to chief controller.

sentences.zh: 其後外州駐紮，又有御前諸軍都統製之名。

translations.literal: Later, when troops were garrisoned in outer prefectures, there was also the title of chief controller of all armies before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when troops were garrisoned in outer prefectures, there was also the title of chief controller of all imperial-front armies.

sentences.zh: 又並入神武軍，以舊統製、統領改充殿前司統製、統領官。

translations.literal: They were also merged into the Divine Martial Army, and the former controllers and leaders were reassigned as controllers and leaders of the Bureau of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: They were also merged into the Divine Martial Army, and the former controllers and leaders were reassigned as controllers and leaders of the Bureau of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，臣僚言：「三衙軍製名稱不正，以舊制論之，軍職大者凡八等，除都指揮使或不常置外，曰殿前副都指揮使、馬軍副都指揮使、步軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao era, officials said: "The names of the Three Commands' military system are incorrect. Under the old system, the great military posts numbered eight grades in all. Apart from the commander-in-chief, who might not always be appointed, they were: palace vice commander-in-chief, cavalry vice commander-in-chief, and infantry vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiandao era, officials said: "The titles of the Three Commands' military system are incorrect. Under the old system, the senior military posts numbered eight grades in all. Apart from the commander-in-chief, who was not always appointed, they were the palace vice commander-in-chief, the cavalry vice commander-in-chief, and the infantry vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 次各有都虞候，次有捧日、天武四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: Next came the chief inspectors; next the commanders-in-chief of the four wings of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the chief inspectors, and next the commanders-in-chief of the four wings of Sun-bearer and Heaven's Martial.

sentences.zh: 龍、神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: Then the commanders-in-chief of the four wings of Dragon and Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the commanders-in-chief of the four wings of Dragon and Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 秩秩有序，若登第然。

translations.literal: The ranks were orderly, like steps on a ladder.
translations.idiomatic: The ranks stood in clear order, like rungs on a ladder.

sentences.zh: 降此而下，則分營、分廂各置副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Below these, each camp and each wing had its own vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Below these, each camp and each wing had its own vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 邊境有事，命將討捕，則旋立總管、鈐轄、都監之名，使各將其所部以出，事已復初。

translations.literal: When the border had trouble and generals were ordered to pursue and suppress, titles of overall commander, supervisory commissioner, and chief overseer were temporarily created so that each led his own unit out; when the affair ended, things returned to the original state.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble arose on the frontier and generals were ordered to pursue and suppress it, titles of overall commander, supervisory commissioner, and chief overseer were temporarily created so that each led his own unit into the field; when the affair ended, the system returned to normal.

sentences.zh: 今以宿衛虎士而與在外諸軍同其名，以統製、統領為之長，又使遙帶外路總管、鈐轄，皆非舊典。

translations.literal: Now palace-guard elite troops share names with armies stationed outside, with controllers and leaders as their chiefs, and they are also made to hold from afar the titles of overall commander and supervisory commissioner on outer circuits—none of this follows the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Now palace-guard elite troops share titles with armies stationed outside, with controllers and leaders as their chiefs, and they are also made to hold from afar the titles of overall commander and supervisory commissioner on outer circuits—none of this follows the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 所當法祖宗之舊，正三衙之名，改諸軍為諸廂，改統製以下為都虞候、指揮使，要使宿衛之職，預有差等，士卒之心，明有所係，異時拜將，必無一軍皆驚之舉。」

translations.literal: We ought to follow the ancestors' old system, correct the names of the Three Commands, change 'armies' to 'wings,' and change controllers and below to chief inspectors and commanders, so that palace-guard duties have clear gradations in advance, soldiers' hearts have a clear object of attachment, and when generals are appointed later there will certainly not be a shock in which an entire army is startled at once."
translations.idiomatic: We ought to follow the ancestors' old system, correct the names of the Three Commands, change 'armies' to 'wings,' and change controllers and below to chief inspectors and commanders, so that palace-guard duties have clear gradations in advance, soldiers know clearly to whom they belong, and when generals are appointed later there will not be a shock in which an entire army is startled at once."

sentences.zh: 時不果行。

translations.literal: At the time this was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 淳熙以後，四廂之職多虛，而殿司職、司有權管幹，有時暫照管之號，愈非乾道以前之比矣。

translations.literal: After Chunxi, posts in the four wings were often vacant, while the palace bureau had acting supervisors and temporary caretaker titles—ever less comparable to the period before Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: After Chunxi, posts in the four wings were often vacant, while the palace bureau had acting supervisors and temporary caretaker titles—ever less comparable to the period before Qiandao.

sentences.zh: 【侍衛親軍馬軍】都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候各一人，掌馬軍諸指揮之名籍，凡統製、訓練、番衛、戌守、遷補、賞罰，皆總其政今；

translations.literal: Imperial Guard Cavalry: one commander-in-chief, one vice commander-in-chief, and one chief inspector each; they managed the registers of all cavalry commands, and oversaw all policies for command, training, rotation of guard duty, garrison service, promotion and transfer, and rewards and punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard Cavalry: there was one commander-in-chief, one vice commander-in-chief, and one chief inspector. They kept the registers of all cavalry commands and oversaw every matter of command, training, guard rotation, garrison duty, promotion and transfer, and rewards and punishments;

sentences.zh: 侍衛扈從，及大禮宿衛，所掌如殿前司官。

translations.literal: they attended and escorted on guard duty, and on great ceremonies managed night watch—duties like those of the Bureau of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: they attended and escorted on guard duty, and on state ceremonies managed night watch, with duties like those of the Bureau of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 所領馬軍，自龍衛而下有左右四廂都指揮使，龍衛左右廂各有都指揮使。

translations.literal: The cavalry under their command, from Dragon Guard downward, had commanders-in-chief over the left and right four wings; each left and right wing of Dragon Guard had its own commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry under their command, from Dragon Guard downward, had commanders-in-chief over the left and right four wings, and each wing of Dragon Guard had its own commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 每軍有都指揮使、都虞候，每指揮有指揮使、副指揮使，每都有軍使、副兵馬使、十將、將虞候、承勾、押官，各以其職隸於馬軍司。

translations.literal: Each army had a commander-in-chief and chief inspector; each command had a commander and vice commander; each company had an army officer, vice horse-and-arms officer, squad leader of ten, officer-inspector, clerk, and escort officer—all subordinate to the Cavalry Command according to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had a commander-in-chief and chief inspector; each command had a commander and vice commander; each company had an army officer, vice horse-and-arms officer, squad leader of ten, officer-inspector, clerk, and escort officer, all subordinate to the Cavalry Command according to their duties.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，詔以馬軍都指揮使、馬軍副都指揮使在正任觀察使之上，馬軍都虞候在正任防禦使之上。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe, an edict placed the cavalry commander-in-chief and cavalry vice commander-in-chief above a regular commissioner of observation, and the cavalry chief inspector above a regular commissioner of defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1114, an edict placed the cavalry commander-in-chief and vice commander-in-chief above a regular commissioner of observation, and the cavalry chief inspector above a regular commissioner of defense.

sentences.zh: 中興後。

translations.literal: After the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration.

sentences.zh: 置主管侍衛馬軍司一員。

translations.literal: One officer was appointed as supervisor of the Imperial Guard Cavalry Command.
translations.idiomatic: One officer was appointed to supervise the Imperial Guard Cavalry Command.

sentences.zh: 其屬有幹辦公事、淮備差遣、點檢醫藥飯食各一員。

translations.literal: Its subordinates included one handler of routine business, one reserve dispatch officer, and one inspector of medicine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff included one handler of routine business, one reserve dispatch officer, and one inspector of medicine and food.

sentences.zh: 掌出戌建康，差主管機宜文字一員，掌馬軍之政令。

translations.literal: It managed deployment to garrison Jiankang and assigned one confidential-documents supervisor; it governed the cavalry command's policies.
translations.idiomatic: It managed deployment to garrison Jiankang and assigned one confidential-documents supervisor, and it governed the cavalry command's policies.

sentences.zh: 凡出入扈衛、守宿以奉上，開收閱習、轉補以勵下，如殿前司。

translations.literal: For all going out and in on escort, night watch to serve above, opening and closing drill and review and transfers to encourage below—it was like the Bureau of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: For escort duty going out and in, night watch to serve the throne, and opening and closing drill, review, and transfers to encourage the ranks, its duties were like those of the Bureau of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 凡名籍核其在亡，過則以法繩之，有巡防敕應，則糾率差撥龍衛四廂隸焉。

translations.literal: For all registers it verified who was present or absent; for offenses it punished according to law; when there were patrol-defense edict responses, it inspected and assigned detachments—the four wings of Dragon Guard were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: It verified registers of who was present or absent, punished offenses according to law, and when patrol-defense edict responses were issued, it inspected and assigned detachments; the four wings of Dragon Guard were subordinate to it.

sentences.zh: 【侍衛親軍步軍】都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候各一人。

translations.literal: Imperial Guard Infantry: one commander-in-chief, one vice commander-in-chief, and one chief inspector each.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard Infantry: there was one commander-in-chief, one vice commander-in-chief, and one chief inspector.

sentences.zh: 掌步軍諸指揮之名籍，凡統製、訓練、番衛、戌守、遷補、賞罰，皆總其政令；

translations.literal: They managed the registers of all infantry commands, and oversaw all policies for command, training, rotation of guard duty, garrison service, promotion and transfer, and rewards and punishments;
translations.idiomatic: They kept the registers of all infantry commands and oversaw every matter of command, training, guard rotation, garrison duty, promotion and transfer, and rewards and punishments;

sentences.zh: 侍衛扈從，及大禮宿衛，如殿前司。

translations.literal: they attended and escorted on guard duty, and on great ceremonies managed night watch, as in the Bureau of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: they attended and escorted on guard duty, and on state ceremonies managed night watch, as in the Bureau of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 所領步軍、自神衛而下有左右四廂都指揮使，左右廂各有都指揮使。

translations.literal: The infantry under their command, from Divine Guard downward, had commanders-in-chief over the left and right four wings; each left and right wing had its own commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry under their command, from Divine Guard downward, had commanders-in-chief over the left and right four wings, and each wing had its own commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 每軍有都指揮使、都虞候，每指揮有指揮使、副指揮使、每都有都頭、副都頭、十將、將、虞候、承勾、押官，各以其職隸於步軍司。

translations.literal: Each army had a commander-in-chief and chief inspector; each command had a commander and vice commander; each company had a company head, vice company head, squad leader of ten, officer, inspector, clerk, and escort officer—all subordinate to the Infantry Command according to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had a commander-in-chief and chief inspector; each command had a commander and vice commander; each company had a company head, vice company head, squad leader of ten, officer, inspector, clerk, and escort officer, all subordinate to the Infantry Command according to their duties.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，詔以步軍都指揮使、步軍副都指揮使在正任觀察使之上，都虞候在正任防禦使之上。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe, an edict placed the infantry commander-in-chief and infantry vice commander-in-chief above a regular commissioner of observation, and the chief inspector above a regular commissioner of defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1114, an edict placed the infantry commander-in-chief and vice commander-in-chief above a regular commissioner of observation, and the chief inspector above a regular commissioner of defense.

sentences.zh: 中興後，置主管侍衛步軍司一員。

translations.literal: After the restoration, one officer was appointed as supervisor of the Imperial Guard Infantry Command.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, one officer was appointed to supervise the Imperial Guard Infantry Command.

sentences.zh: 其屬有幹辦公事二員。

translations.literal: Its subordinates included two handlers of routine business.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff included two handlers of routine business.

sentences.zh: 淮備差遣、點檢醫藥飯食各一員，掌步軍之政令。

translations.literal: One reserve dispatch officer and one inspector of medicine and food; it governed the infantry command's policies.
translations.idiomatic: There was one reserve dispatch officer and one inspector of medicine and food, and it governed the infantry command's policies.

sentences.zh: 凡出入扈衛、守宿以奉上，開收閱習、轉補以勵下，如殿前司。

translations.literal: For all going out and in on escort, night watch to serve above, opening and closing drill and review and transfers to encourage below—it was like the Bureau of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: For escort duty going out and in, night watch to serve the throne, and opening and closing drill, review, and transfers to encourage the ranks, its duties were like those of the Bureau of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 凡名籍校其在亡，過則以法繩之，有巡防敕應，則糾率差撥神衛四廂隸焉。

translations.literal: For all registers it checked who was present or absent; for offenses it punished according to law; when there were patrol-defense edict responses, it inspected and assigned detachments—the four wings of Divine Guard were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: It checked registers of who was present or absent, punished offenses according to law, and when patrol-defense edict responses were issued, it inspected and assigned detachments; the four wings of Divine Guard were subordinate to it.

sentences.zh: 【環衛官】左、右金吾衛上將軍大將軍將軍中郎將郎將左、右衛上將軍大將軍將軍中郎將郎將左、右驍衛上將軍大將軍將軍

translations.literal: Palace Guard ranks: Left and Right Golden Crow Guards: senior general, great general, general, middle commander, and gentleman-commander; Left and Right Guards: senior general, great general, general, middle commander, and gentleman-commander; Left and Right Valiant Guards: senior general, great general, and general.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard ranks: for the Left and Right Golden Crow Guards, senior general, great general, general, middle commander, and gentleman-commander; for the Left and Right Guards, senior general, great general, general, middle commander, and gentleman-commander; for the Left and Right Valiant Guards, senior general, great general, and general.

sentences.zh: 左、右武衛上將軍大將軍將軍左、右屯衛上將軍大將軍將軍左、右領軍衛上將軍大將軍將軍左、右監門衛上將軍大將軍將軍

translations.literal: Left and Right Martial Guards: senior general, great general, and general; Left and Right Garrison Guards: senior general, great general, and general; Left and Right Army-leader Guards: senior general, great general, and general; Left and Right Gate-watch Guards: senior general, great general, and general.
translations.idiomatic: For the Left and Right Martial Guards: senior general, great general, and general; for the Left and Right Garrison Guards: senior general, great general, and general; for the Left and Right Army-leader Guards: senior general, great general, and general; for the Left and Right Gate-watch Guards: senior general, great general, and general.

sentences.zh: 左、右千牛衛上將軍大將軍將軍中郎將郎將

translations.literal: Left and Right Thousand-Ox Guards: senior general, great general, general, middle commander, and gentleman-commander.
translations.idiomatic: For the Left and Right Thousand-Ox Guards: senior general, great general, general, middle commander, and gentleman-commander.

sentences.zh: 諸衛上將軍、大將軍、將軍，並為環衛官，無定員，皆命宗室為之，亦為武臣之贈典。

translations.literal: The senior generals, great generals, and generals of all guards were all Palace Guard ranks, with no fixed quota; all were appointed from the imperial clan, and they also served as honorary titles for military officials.
translations.idiomatic: The senior generals, great generals, and generals of all guards were Palace Guard ranks with no fixed quota. They were normally filled by members of the imperial clan and also served as honorary titles for military officials.

sentences.zh: 大將軍以下，又為武官責降散官。

translations.literal: Great general and below were also used as demoted honorary ranks for military officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks from great general downward were also used as demoted honorary ranks for military officials.

sentences.zh: 政和中，改武臣官制，而環衛如故，蓋雖有四十八階，別無所領故也。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era the military-official rank system was changed, but the Palace Guard ranks remained as before, because although there were forty-eight grades, they commanded nothing in particular.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era the military-official rank system was changed, but the Palace Guard ranks remained as before, because although there were forty-eight grades, they had no actual command responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔以武安軍節度使錢景臻等為左金吾衛上將軍，保信軍節度使劉敷等為右金吾衛上將軍，用御史中丞陳過庭言，遵藝祖開寶初罷王彥超、武行德等歸環衛故事也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict appointed Qian Jingzhen, military commissioner of Wu'an Army, and others as senior generals of the Left Golden Crow Guard, and Liu Fu, military commissioner of Baoxin Army, and others as senior generals of the Right Golden Crow Guard, following the memorial of Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Guoting and observing the precedent of the founding ancestor in early Kaibao, when Wang Yanchao, Wu Xingde, and others were removed and returned to Palace Guard ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1126, an edict appointed Qian Jingzhen, military commissioner of Wu'an Army, and others as senior generals of the Left Golden Crow Guard, and Liu Fu, military commissioner of Baoxin Army, and others as senior generals of the Right Golden Crow Guard, following Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Guoting's memorial and observing the precedent of the founding ancestor in early Kaibao, when Wang Yanchao, Wu Xingde, and others were removed and returned to Palace Guard ranks.

sentences.zh: 其禁兵分隸殿前及侍衛兩司，所稱十二衛將軍，皆空官無實，中興多不除授。

translations.literal: The forbidden troops were divided between the Bureau of the Palace Command and the two Imperial Guard commands; the so-called generals of the twelve guards were all empty titles without substance, and after the restoration they were mostly not appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The forbidden troops were divided between the Bureau of the Palace Command and the two Imperial Guard commands; the so-called generals of the twelve guards were empty titles without substance, and after the restoration they were mostly not appointed.

sentences.zh: 隆興中，始命學士洪遵等討論典故，復置十六衛，號環衛官。

translations.literal: In the Longxing era, Academician Hong Zun and others were first ordered to examine historical precedents and restore the sixteen guards, titled Palace Guard ranks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longxing era, Academician Hong Zun and others were first ordered to examine historical precedents and restore the sixteen guards under the title of Palace Guard ranks.

sentences.zh: 其法：節度使則領左、右金吾衛上將軍，承宣使則領左、右衛上將軍，在內則兼帶，在外則不帶；

translations.literal: The rule was: a military commissioner held the senior generalship of the Left and Right Golden Crow Guards; a commissioner of promotion held the senior generalship of the Left and Right Guards; if within the capital he held it concurrently, if outside he did not;
translations.idiomatic: The rule was that a military commissioner held the senior generalship of the Left and Right Golden Crow Guards, and a commissioner of promotion held the senior generalship of the Left and Right Guards; if he was in the capital he held the title concurrently, but if he was posted outside he did not.

sentences.zh: 正任為上將軍，遙郡為大將軍，正親兄弟子孫試充。

translations.literal: a regular appointment was senior general, a distant prefecture was great general, and legitimate brothers' sons and grandsons were tried out in the posts.
translations.idiomatic: A regular appointment carried the title of senior general, a distant prefecture carried great general, and legitimate brothers' sons and grandsons were tried out in the posts.

sentences.zh: 又詔祖宗諸後自明肅至欽慈諸後及后妃嬪御之家，各具本宗堪充諸衛官以名銜聞。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered the various imperial consorts from Mingsu through Qinci and the families of empresses, consorts, and palace women each to report by name and title those in their clans fit to fill guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered the various imperial consorts from Mingsu through Qinci and the families of empresses, consorts, and palace women each to report by name and title those in their clans fit to fill guard posts.

sentences.zh: 又詔三衛郎為三衛侍郎。

translations.literal: An edict also changed Three Guards gentleman to Three Guards vice director.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also changed the title Three Guards gentleman to Three Guards vice director.

sentences.zh: 又詔博士並差文臣。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered that all instructors be assigned from among civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered that all instructors be assigned from among civil officials.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年二月置，五年正月罷。

translations.literal: Established in the second month of the fourth year of Chongning; abolished in the first month of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was established in the second month of 1105 and abolished in the first month of 1106.

sentences.zh: 【皇城司】幹當官七人，以武功大夫以上及內侍都知、押班充。

translations.literal: Imperial City Bureau: seven acting officers, filled by Grandee of Martial Achievement and above and by chief stewards and escort shift leaders of the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial City Bureau: there were seven acting officers, filled by officials of Grandee of Martial Achievement rank and above and by chief stewards and escort shift leaders of the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 掌宮城出入之禁令，凡周廬宿衛之事、宮門啟閉之節皆隸焉。

translations.literal: They managed prohibitions on entry and exit from the palace city; all encircling-garrison night-watch duties and the rules for opening and closing palace gates were subordinate to them.
translations.idiomatic: They enforced prohibitions on entry and exit from the palace city, and all encircling-garrison night-watch duties and the rules for opening and closing palace gates were subordinate to them.

sentences.zh: 每門給銅符二、鐵牌一，左符留門，右符請鑰，鐵牌則請鑰者自隨，以時參驗而啟閉之。

translations.literal: Each gate was issued two bronze tallies and one iron plaque; the left tally remained at the gate, the right tally was presented to request the key, and the iron plaque was carried by the key-requester himself; at the proper time they were checked together to open and close.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate was issued two bronze tallies and one iron plaque. The left tally remained at the gate, the right tally was presented to request the key, and the iron plaque was carried by whoever requested the key; at the proper time they were checked together before the gate was opened or closed.

sentences.zh: 總親從、親事官名籍，辨其宿衛之地，以均其番直。

translations.literal: They maintained the registers of intimate attendants and personal-service officers, distinguished their night-watch stations, and equalized their rotation shifts.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained the registers of intimate attendants and personal-service officers, assigned their night-watch stations, and equalized their rotation shifts.

sentences.zh: 人物偽冒不應法，則譏察以聞。

translations.literal: If persons impersonated others or violated the law, they investigated and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: If persons impersonated others or violated the regulations, they investigated and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 凡臣僚朝覲，上下馬有定所，自宰相、親王以下，所帶人從有定數，揭榜以止其喧哄。

translations.literal: For all officials attending court audience, mounting and dismounting had fixed places; from the chief minister and imperial princes downward, the number of attendants they brought had a fixed quota; placards were posted to stop disorderly clamor.
translations.idiomatic: For all officials attending court audience, mounting and dismounting had fixed places. From the chief minister and imperial princes downward, the number of attendants they brought had a fixed quota, and placards were posted to stop disorderly clamor.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，詔幹當皇城司，除兩省都知、押班外，取年深者減罷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, an edict on acting officers of the Imperial City Bureau ordered that, apart from chief stewards and escort shift leaders of the two inner bureaus, those of long service be reduced and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1083, an edict on acting officers of the Imperial City Bureau ordered that, apart from chief stewards and escort shift leaders of the two inner bureaus, those of long service be reduced and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 止留十員。

translations.literal: Only ten posts were retained.
translations.idiomatic: Only ten posts were retained.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，詔幹當官閱三年無過者遷秩一等，再任滿者減磨勘二年。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, an edict said that acting officers who completed three years without fault were promoted one rank, and those who completed a second full term had two years deducted from their merit review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086, an edict said that acting officers who completed three years without fault were promoted one rank, and those who completed a second full term had two years deducted from their merit review.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，詔：「應宮城出入請納官物，呈稟公事，傳送文書，並禦廚、翰林、儀鸞司非次祗應，聽於便門出入，即不由所定門者，論如闌入律。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, an edict said: "For entry and exit from the palace city to request delivery of official goods, present routine business, transmit documents, and extraordinary service for the Imperial Kitchen, Hanlin Academy, and Ceremonial Insignia Bureau, passage through convenience gates is permitted; if one does not use the designated gate, it is prosecuted under the statute on unlawful entry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1098, an edict said: "For entry and exit from the palace city to deliver official goods, present routine business, transmit documents, and provide extraordinary service for the Imperial Kitchen, Hanlin Academy, and Ceremonial Insignia Bureau, passage through convenience gates is permitted; if one does not use the designated gate, the case is prosecuted under the statute on unlawful entry.

sentences.zh: 應差辦人物入內，及內諸司差人往他所應奉，並前一日具名數與經歷諸門報皇城司。」

translations.literal: Persons assigned to enter on errands, and inner bureaus assigning persons to other places on service, must all list names and numbers the day before and report to the Imperial City Bureau through the gates they pass."
translations.idiomatic: Persons assigned to enter on errands, and inner bureaus assigning persons to other places on service, had to list names and numbers the day before and report to the Imperial City Bureau through the gates they passed."

sentences.zh: 二年，詔皇城司任滿酬獎依熙寧五年指揮，再任滿無遺闕，取旨。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict said that rewards on completing a term in the Imperial City Bureau followed the directive of the fifth year of Xining; if a second term was completed without omission, imperial instruction was to be sought.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, an edict said that rewards on completing a term in the Imperial City Bureau followed the directive of 1072; if a second term was completed without omission, imperial instruction was to be sought.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，詔皇城司可創置親從弟五指揮，以七百人為額，

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, an edict permitted the Imperial City Bureau to newly establish five companies of intimate-attendant younger brothers, with a quota of seven hundred men,
translations.idiomatic: In 1115, an edict permitted the Imperial City Bureau to establish five companies of intimate-attendant younger brothers, with a quota of seven hundred men,

sentences.zh: 〈（親從官舊有四指揮，元額共二千二百七十人，）〉

translations.literal: (The intimate-attendant offices formerly had four companies, with an original quota of 2,270 men in all.)
translations.idiomatic: (The intimate-attendant offices formerly had four companies, with an original quota of 2,270 men in all.)

sentences.zh: 仍以五尺九寸一分六厘使為將軍，副使為中郎將，使臣以下為左、右郎將，通以十員為額，宗室不在此例。

translations.literal: Envoys of five chi nine cun one fen six li were still made generals, vice-envoys middle commanders, and envoys and below Left and Right gentleman-commanders, with a total quota of ten posts; imperial clansmen were not included in this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys of five chi nine cun one fen six li were still made generals, vice-envoys middle commanders, and envoys and below Left and Right gentleman-commanders, with a total quota of ten posts; members of the imperial clan were excluded from this rule.

sentences.zh: 除管軍則解，或領閣門、皇城之類則仍帶，雖戚裏子弟，非戰功人不除，批書印紙屬殿前司。

translations.literal: If one took command of troops the title was removed; if one held Gate office, Imperial City office, or the like, it was still carried concurrently. Even sons of imperial affines were not appointed without military merit; the endorsement documents belonged to the Bureau of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: If one took command of troops the title was removed; if one held Gate office, Imperial City office, or the like, it was still carried concurrently. Even sons of imperial affines were not appointed without military merit, and the endorsement documents belonged to the Bureau of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝諭宰相，以為如文臣館閣儲才之地。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor told the chief ministers that it was like the civil officials' Hall and Pavilion as a place to store talent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor told the chief ministers that it was like the civil officials' Hall and Pavilion as a place to cultivate talent.

sentences.zh: 紹熙初，嘗欲留闕以儲將才，循初意也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxi, he once wished to leave vacancies to store military talent, following the original intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaoxi, he once wished to leave vacancies open to cultivate military talent, following the original intent.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰中，復申明隆興之詔，屏除貪得妄進，以重環尹之官，嘉定二年，復因臣僚言，專以曾為兵將有功績及名將子孫之有才略者充。

translations.literal: In the Jiatai era the Longxing edict was again proclaimed, greedy and reckless advancement was excluded, and the Palace Guard posts were made weightier; in the second year of Jiading, following officials' memorials, only those who had been military officers with merit and talented descendants of famous generals were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiatai era the Longxing edict was proclaimed again, greedy and reckless advancement was excluded, and the Palace Guard posts were given greater weight; in 1209, following officials' memorials, only those who had been military officers with merit and talented descendants of famous generals were appointed.

sentences.zh: 通前後觀之，可以見環衛儲才之意。

translations.literal: Viewed through from beginning to end, one can see the intent of storing talent in the Palace Guard ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from beginning to end, one can see the intent of using the Palace Guard ranks to cultivate talent.

sentences.zh: 【三衛官】三衛郎一員，秩比太中大夫。

translations.literal: Three Guards offices: one Three Guards gentleman, rank comparable to Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Three Guards offices: one Three Guards gentleman, with rank comparable to Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 中郎為之貳，文武各一員，秩比朝議大夫。

translations.literal: Middle commanders served as his deputies, one civil and one military, rank comparable to Grandee of Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Middle commanders served as his deputies, one civil and one military, with rank comparable to Grandee of Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 博士二員，主簿一員。

translations.literal: Two instructors and one registrar.
translations.idiomatic: There were two instructors and one registrar.

sentences.zh: 親衛府郎十員，中郎十員；

translations.literal: Intimate Guard Bureau: ten gentlemen and ten middle commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Intimate Guard Bureau: ten gentlemen and ten middle commanders;

sentences.zh: 勳衛府郎十員，中郎十員；

translations.literal: Merit Guard Bureau: ten gentlemen and ten middle commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Merit Guard Bureau: ten gentlemen and ten middle commanders;

sentences.zh: 翊衛府郎二十員，中郎二十員；

translations.literal: Assistant Guard Bureau: twenty gentlemen and twenty middle commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Guard Bureau: twenty gentlemen and twenty middle commanders;

sentences.zh: 文武各四十員。

translations.literal: forty civil and forty military posts in all.
translations.idiomatic: forty civil and forty military posts in all.

sentences.zh: 三衛郎治其府之事。

translations.literal: The Three Guards gentleman managed the affairs of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Guards gentleman managed the affairs of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 率其屬日直於殿陛，長在左，立起居郎之前；

translations.literal: He led his subordinates on daily duty at the throne hall; the chief stood on the left, before the attendance recorder;
translations.idiomatic: He led his subordinates on daily duty at the throne hall; the chief stood on the left, before the attendance recorder;

sentences.zh: 貳分左右，文東武西，立都承旨之後，仗退，治事於府。

translations.literal: the deputies stood left and right, civil east and military west, behind the chief usher; when the guard formation withdrew, they handled business at the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: the deputies stood left and right, civil on the east and military on the west, behind the chief usher; when the guard formation withdrew, they handled business at the bureau.

sentences.zh: 博士掌孝道，校試三衛所習文武之藝。

translations.literal: The instructors managed filial conduct and examined and tested the civil and military arts studied by the Three Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The instructors managed filial conduct and examined the civil and military arts studied by the Three Guards.

sentences.zh: 親衛立於殿上兩旁，勳衛立於朵殿，翊衛立於兩階衛士之前。

translations.literal: Intimate Guards stood on both sides of the upper hall, Merit Guards stood in the side hall, and Assistant Guards stood before the guards on the two stairways.
translations.idiomatic: Intimate Guards stood on both sides of the upper hall, Merit Guards stood in the side hall, and Assistant Guards stood before the guards on the two stairways.

sentences.zh: 三衛郎依給、舍，中郎依少卿，餘依寺丞。

translations.literal: The Three Guards gentleman followed the model of aides and attendants, middle commanders followed vice directors, and the rest followed bureau assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Guards gentleman followed the model of aides and attendants, middle commanders followed vice directors, and the rest followed bureau assistants.

sentences.zh: 親衛官以后妃嬪御之家有服親，及翰林學士並管軍正任觀察使以上子孫；

translations.literal: Intimate Guard posts were for those with mourning kinship in the families of empresses, consorts, and palace women, and for descendants of Hanlin academicians and of regular military commissioners of observation rank and above who commanded troops;
translations.idiomatic: Intimate Guard posts were for those with mourning kinship in the families of empresses, consorts, and palace women, and for descendants of Hanlin academicians and of regular military commissioners of observation rank and above who commanded troops;

sentences.zh: 勳衛官以勳臣之世、賢德之後有服親，太中大夫以上及正任團練使、遙郡觀察使以上；

translations.literal: Merit Guard posts were for those with mourning kinship in lines of merit officials and virtuous descendants, for Grandees of Splendid Happiness and above, and for regular commissioners of regimentation and distant-prefecture commissioners of observation and above;
translations.idiomatic: Merit Guard posts were for those with mourning kinship in lines of merit officials and virtuous descendants, for Grandees of Splendid Happiness and above, and for regular commissioners of regimentation and distant-prefecture commissioners of observation and above;

sentences.zh: 翊衛官以卿監、正任刺史、遙郡團練使以上，並以為等。

translations.literal: Assistant Guard posts were for director-level officials, regular prefectural commissioners, and distant-prefecture commissioners of regimentation and above; these were taken as the grades.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Guard posts were for director-level officials, regular prefectural commissioners, and distant-prefecture commissioners of regimentation and above; these were taken as the qualifying grades.

sentences.zh: 其將校、十將、節級等應合行事件，比第四指揮及見行條貫。

translations.literal: For their officers, squad leaders of ten, rank markers, and other matters to be carried out, they were compared to the fourth command and current regulations.
translations.idiomatic: For their officers, squad leaders of ten, rank markers, and other applicable matters, they followed the fourth command and current regulations.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，應臣僚輒帶售雇人入宮門，罪賞並依宗室法，將帶過數止坐本官，若兼領外局，所定人從非隨本官輒入者，依闌入法。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, for officials who casually brought hired servants into palace gates, rewards and punishments all followed the law for the imperial clan; if the number brought exceeded the limit, only the official's own post was penalized; if one concurrently held an outer bureau, and the fixed attendants not following the official's own post entered casually, it was prosecuted under the statute on unlawful entry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year, officials who casually brought hired servants into palace gates were rewarded or punished according to the law for the imperial clan; if the number brought exceeded the limit, only the official's own post was penalized; if one concurrently held an outer bureau and fixed attendants not attached to the official's own post entered casually, the case was prosecuted under the statute on unlawful entry.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔嘉王楷差提舉皇城司整肅隨駕禁衛所。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict assigned Prince Jia Kai to supervise the Imperial City Bureau in rectifying the forbidden-guard posts accompanying the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, an edict assigned Prince Jia Kai to supervise the Imperial City Bureau in rectifying the forbidden-guard posts accompanying the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔應入皇城門，依法服本色，輒衣便服及不裹頭帽入出者並科罪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict said that those entering the imperial city gate must wear regulated service colors by law; those who wore casual dress or entered and exited without wrapped headgear were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1126, an edict required those entering the imperial city gate to wear regulated service colors; those who wore casual dress or entered and exited without wrapped headgear were all punished.

sentences.zh: 所隸官屬一：冰井務，掌藏冰以薦獻宗廟、供奉禁庭及邦國之用。

translations.literal: Subordinate office 1: Ice Well Office, which stored ice for offerings to the ancestral temples, service to the forbidden court, and state use.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate office 1: the Ice Well Office, which stored ice for offerings to the ancestral temples, service to the forbidden court, and state use.

sentences.zh: 若賜予臣下，則以法式頒之。

translations.literal: If bestowed on officials below, it was distributed according to statutory formulas.
translations.idiomatic: If bestowed on officials below, it was distributed according to statutory formulas.

sentences.zh: 中興初，爲行營禁衞所，差主管官，掌出入皇城宮殿門等敕號，察其假冒，車駕行幸則糾察導從。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the restoration it became the Traveling Camp Forbidden Guard Office, with a supervising officer appointed to manage entry and exit at imperial city and palace gates and credential tokens, inspect for impersonation, and on imperial outings inspect the escort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the restoration it became the Traveling Camp Forbidden Guard Office, with a supervising officer to manage palace-gate credentials, detect impersonation, and inspect escorts on imperial outings.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，改稱行在皇城司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing it was renamed the Traveling Imperial City Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 it was renamed the Traveling Imperial City Bureau.

sentences.zh: 提舉官一員，提點官二員，幹當官五員，以諸司副使、内侍都知押班充。

translations.literal: There was one supervisory commissioner, two inspection commissioners, and five acting officers, filled by vice commissioners of various bureaus and chief stewards and escort shift leaders of the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: It had one supervisory commissioner, two inspection commissioners, and five acting officers drawn from bureau vice commissioners and Inner Service chief stewards and escort shift leaders.

sentences.zh: 掌皇城宮殿門，給三色牌號，稽驗出入。

translations.literal: It managed imperial city and palace gates, issued three-color tally tokens, and inspected entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: It managed imperial city and palace gates, issued three-color tally tokens, and inspected all entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 凡親從，親事官五指揮，入内院子、守闕入内院子指揮，總其名籍，均其勞役，察其功過而賞罰之。

translations.literal: For all intimate attendants, five companies of intimate-service officers, Inner Palace Courtyard commands, and reserve Inner Palace Courtyard commands, it kept the registers, equalized labor service, and inspected merit and fault for rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: It kept registers of intimate attendants, five intimate-service companies, Inner Palace Courtyard commands, and reserve Inner Palace Courtyard commands, equalized their labor, and rewarded or punished them according to merit and fault.

sentences.zh: 凡諸門必謹所守；

translations.literal: Every gate had to guard its post carefully;
translations.idiomatic: Every gate had to guard its post carefully;

sentences.zh: 蠲潔齊肅，郊祀大禮，則差撥隨從守衞；

translations.literal: for purification and solemn preparation at suburban sacrifices and great ceremonies, escort guards were assigned;
translations.idiomatic: for suburban sacrifices and great ceremonies it assigned escort guards;

sentences.zh: 有宴設，則守門約闌。

translations.literal: when banquets were set, gatekeepers controlled access.
translations.idiomatic: and for banquets it controlled gate access.

sentences.zh: 毎年春秋，按賞親從逐指揮、親事官第一指揮、長行三色武藝、弓弩槍手。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn it reviewed and rewarded intimate-attendant companies, the first intimate-service company, rank-and-file three-color martial skills, and bow, crossbow, and spear troops.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn it reviewed and rewarded intimate-attendant companies, the first intimate-service company, rank-and-file three-color martial skills, and bow, crossbow, and spear troops.

sentences.zh: 皇城周回或有墊陷，移文修整。

translations.literal: If the imperial city perimeter sank or collapsed anywhere, documents were sent to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial city perimeter sank or collapsed, repair orders were issued.

sentences.zh: 嘉定間，臣僚言：「皇城一司，總率親從，嚴護周盧，參錯禁旅，權亞殿嚴，乞專以知閣、御帶兼領。

translations.literal: In the Jiading era, officials memorialized: "The Imperial City Bureau commands intimate attendants, strictly protects the perimeter, overlaps with the forbidden guard, and ranks just below palace guard; we beg that it be led exclusively by Gate managers and Imperial Bearers concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiading, officials memorialized: "The Imperial City Bureau commands intimate attendants, protects the perimeter, overlaps with the forbidden guard, and ranks just below palace guard; we ask that Gate managers and Imperial Bearers lead it exclusively.

sentences.zh: 仍立定親從員額，以革泛監。」

translations.literal: Fixed quotas for intimate attendants should also be established to end indiscriminate supervision."
translations.idiomatic: Fixed intimate-attendant quotas should also be set to end indiscriminate supervision."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: The court approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 客省使、副使各二人。

translations.literal: The Reception Bureau had two commissioners and two vice commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The Reception Bureau had two commissioners and two vice commissioners.

sentences.zh: 掌國信使見辭宴賜及四方進奉、四夷朝覲貢獻之儀，受其幣而賓禮之，掌其饔餼欽食，還則頒詔書，授以賜予。

translations.literal: They managed audiences, farewells, banquets, and gifts for state envoys, and the ceremonies for tribute from the four directions and audiences and offerings from the four barbarians; they received their gifts and treated them as guests, managed their feasts and food and drink, and on their return issued edicts and conferred grants.
translations.idiomatic: They managed audiences, farewells, banquets, and gifts for state envoys, and the ceremonies for tribute from the four directions and audiences and offerings from foreign peoples; they received their gifts and treated them as guests, managed their feasts and provisions, and on their return issued edicts and conferred grants.

sentences.zh: 宰臣以下節物，則視其品秩以為等。

translations.literal: For seasonal gifts to the chief minister and below, they determined grades according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: For seasonal gifts to the chief minister and below, they determined grades according to rank.

sentences.zh: 若文臣中散大夫、武臣橫行刺史以上還闕朝覲，掌賜酒饌。

translations.literal: When civil officials of Palace Attendant rank and military officials of transverse prefectural commissioner rank and above returned to court for audience, they managed the bestowal of wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: When civil officials of Palace Attendant rank and military officials of transverse prefectural commissioner rank and above returned to court for audience, they managed the bestowal of wine and food.

sentences.zh: 使闕，則引進、四方館、閤門使副互權。

translations.literal: If a commissioner was vacant, the Introduction Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, and Gate vice commissioners acted for one another by turns.
translations.idiomatic: If a commissioner was vacant, the Introduction Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, and Gate vice commissioners acted for one another by turns.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，詔客省、四方館不隸台察。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, an edict placed the Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel outside censorial oversight.
translations.idiomatic: In 1107, an edict placed the Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel outside censorial oversight.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，改定武選新階，乃詔客省、四方館、引進司、東、西上閤門所掌職務格法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, when the new grades for military selection were fixed, an edict ordered the statutory formats for duties managed by the Reception Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, Introduction Bureau, and Eastern and Western Upper Gate offices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1112, when the new grades for military selection were fixed, an edict ordered the statutory formats for duties managed by the Reception Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, Introduction Bureau, and Eastern and Western Upper Gate offices.

sentences.zh: 並令尚書省具上。

translations.literal: All were ordered submitted in full by the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: All were to be submitted in full by the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 又詔高麗已稱國信，改隸客省。

translations.literal: An edict also said that since Goryeo was already styled a state envoy, it was reassigned to the Reception Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also said that since Goryeo was already styled a state envoy, it was reassigned to the Reception Bureau.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔客省、引進司、四方館、西上閤門為殿庭應奉，與東上閤門一同隸中書省，不隸台察。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict placed the Reception Bureau, Introduction Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, and Western Upper Gate as hall service for the throne hall, and together with the Eastern Upper Gate they were subordinated to the Secretariat, not to censorial oversight.
translations.idiomatic: In 1126, an edict placed the Reception Bureau, Introduction Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, and Western Upper Gate as hall service for the throne hall; together with the Eastern Upper Gate they were subordinated to the Secretariat and placed outside censorial oversight.

sentences.zh: 引進司使、副各二人。

translations.literal: Introduction Bureau: two commissioners and two vice commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Introduction Bureau: two commissioners and two vice commissioners.

sentences.zh: 掌臣僚、蕃國進奉禮物之事，班四方館上。

translations.literal: They managed gifts presented by officials and foreign states, ranking above the Four Directions Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: They managed gifts presented by officials and foreign states, ranking above the Four Directions Hostel.

sentences.zh: 使闕，則客省、四方館互兼。

translations.literal: If a commissioner was vacant, the Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel covered for each other.
translations.idiomatic: If a commissioner was vacant, the Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel covered for each other.

sentences.zh: 【四方館使】二人。

translations.literal: Four Directions Hostel commissioners: two.
translations.idiomatic: Four Directions Hostel: two commissioners.

sentences.zh: 掌進章表，凡文武官朝見辭謝、國忌賜香，及諸道元日、冬至、朔旦慶賀起居章表，皆受而進之。

translations.literal: They managed submission of memorials and reports; for all civil and military officials' audiences, farewells, national-mourning incense grants, and New Year's Day, winter solstice, and first-of-month congratulatory attendance reports from all circuits, they received and forwarded them.
translations.idiomatic: They managed submission of memorials and reports; for all civil and military officials' audiences, farewells, national-mourning incense grants, and New Year's Day, winter solstice, and first-of-month congratulatory attendance reports from all circuits, they received and forwarded them.

sentences.zh: 郊祀大朝會，則定外國使命及致仕、未升朝官父老陪位之版，進士、道釋亦如之。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifice and great court assemblies, they fixed the rosters of foreign missions and of retired officials, fathers and elders of officials not yet attending court, and presented graduates, Daoists, and Buddhists likewise.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban sacrifice and great court assemblies, they fixed the rosters of foreign missions and of retired officials, fathers and elders of officials not yet attending court, and presented graduates, Daoists, and Buddhists likewise.

sentences.zh: 掌凡護葬、賻贈、朝拜之事。

translations.literal: They managed all matters of escorting funerals, condolence gifts, and court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: They managed all matters of escorting funerals, condolence gifts, and court audiences.

sentences.zh: 客省、四方館，建炎初並歸東上閤門，皆知閤總之。

translations.literal: The Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel, at the beginning of Jianyan, were both returned to the Eastern Upper Gate, all overseen by the Gate director.
translations.idiomatic: The Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel, at the beginning of Jianyan, were both returned to the Eastern Upper Gate, all overseen by the Gate director.

sentences.zh: 東、西上閤門東上閤門、西上閤門使各三人，副使各二人，宣讚舍人十人，舊名通事閤人，政和中改。

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Upper Gates: three commissioners and two vice commissioners each for Eastern and Western Upper Gate; ten proclamation aides, formerly called gate liaison attendants, renamed in Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Upper Gates: three commissioners and two vice commissioners each; ten proclamation aides, formerly called gate liaison attendants, renamed during Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 祗候十有二人。

translations.literal: Twelve attendants.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve attendants.

sentences.zh: 掌朝會宴幸、供奉讚相禮儀之事，使、副承旨稟命，舍人傳宣讚謁，祗候分佐舍人。

translations.literal: They managed court assemblies, banquets, imperial visits, and service in proclaiming and assisting ceremonial rites; commissioners and vice commissioners received orders and reported upward, aides transmitted proclamations and announced audiences, and attendants assisted the aides in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: They managed court assemblies, banquets, imperial visits, and service in proclaiming and assisting ceremonial rites; commissioners and vice commissioners received orders and reported upward, aides transmitted proclamations and announced audiences, and attendants assisted the aides in divisions.

sentences.zh: 凡文武官自宰臣、宗室自親王、外國自契丹使以下朝見謝辭皆掌之，視其品秩以為引班、敘班之次，讚其拜舞之節而糾其違失。

translations.literal: They managed audiences and farewells for all civil and military officials from the chief minister downward, imperial clansmen from imperial princes downward, and foreigners from Khitan envoys downward; they set the order of leading formations and arranging formations according to rank, proclaimed the rhythms of bowing and dancing, and corrected violations.
translations.idiomatic: They managed audiences and farewells for all civil and military officials from the chief minister downward, imperial clansmen from imperial princes downward, and foreigners from Khitan envoys downward; they set the order of leading and arranging formations according to rank, proclaimed the rhythms of bowing and dancing, and corrected violations.

sentences.zh: 若慶禮奉表，則東上閤門掌之；

translations.literal: For congratulatory rites presenting memorials, the Eastern Upper Gate managed them;
translations.idiomatic: For congratulatory rites presenting memorials, the Eastern Upper Gate managed them;

sentences.zh: 慰禮進名，則西上閤門掌之。

translations.literal: for condolence rites presenting names, the Western Upper Gate managed them.
translations.idiomatic: for condolence rites presenting names, the Western Upper Gate managed them.

sentences.zh: 月進班簿，歳終一易，分東西班掲貼以進。

translations.literal: Monthly they submitted formation registers, replaced once a year at year's end, divided into eastern and western classes and posted for submission.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly they submitted formation registers, replaced once a year at year's end, divided into eastern and western classes and posted for submission.

sentences.zh: 自客省而下，因事建官，皆有定員。

translations.literal: From the Reception Bureau downward, offices were created as tasks required, all with fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: From the Reception Bureau downward, offices were created as tasks required, all with fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 遂立積考序遷之法，聽其領職居外，增置看班祗候六人，由看班遷至使皆五年，使以上七年，遇闕乃遷，無闕則加遙郡。

translations.literal: They then established a law of accumulated review and ordered advancement, permitting them to hold office while residing outside; six formation-viewing attendants were added; from formation-viewing attendant to commissioner was five years, from commissioner upward seven years; advancement came only when there was a vacancy, and if none, a distant prefecture was added.
translations.idiomatic: They then established a law of accumulated review and ordered advancement, permitting them to hold office while residing outside; six formation-viewing attendants were added; from formation-viewing attendant to commissioner took five years, from commissioner upward seven years; advancement came only when there was a vacancy, and if none, a distant prefecture was added.

sentences.zh: 元豐七年，詔客省、四方館使、副領本職外，官最高者一員兼領合門事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng, an edict said that apart from leading their own posts, the highest-ranking commissioner or vice commissioner of the Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel should concurrently manage Gate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1084, an edict said that apart from leading their own posts, the highest-ranking commissioner or vice commissioner of the Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel should concurrently manage Gate affairs.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，詔客省、四方館、閤門並以橫行通領職事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, an edict said that the Reception Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, and Gate were all to be led in common by transverse ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086, an edict said that the Reception Bureau, Four Directions Hostel, and Gate were all to be led in common by transverse ranks.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，詔看班祗候有闕，令吏部選定，尚書省呈人材，中書省取旨差。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, an edict said that when formation-viewing attendants were vacant, the Ministry of Personnel should select candidates, the Ministry of Personnel should present their qualifications, and the Secretariat should appoint by imperial instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1096, an edict said that when formation-viewing attendants were vacant, the Ministry of Personnel should select candidates and present their qualifications, and the Secretariat should appoint by imperial instruction.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年，詔閤門依元豐法隸門下省。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning, an edict placed the Gate under the Chancellery according to the Yuanfeng law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1105, an edict placed the Gate under the Chancellery according to the Yuanfeng law.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，詔閤門依殿中省例，不隸台察。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, an edict placed the Gate under the precedent of the Palace Secretariat, outside censorial oversight.
translations.idiomatic: In 1107, an edict placed the Gate under the precedent of the Palace Secretariat, outside censorial oversight.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，詔宣讚播告，直誦其辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, an edict said that proclamation aides broadcasting announcements should recite the text directly.
translations.idiomatic: In 1116, an edict said that proclamation aides broadcasting announcements should recite the text directly.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔閤門並立員額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict established fixed quotas for the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1126, an edict established fixed quotas for the Gate.

sentences.zh: 監察御史胡舜陟奏：「閤門之職，祖宗所重：宣讚不過三五人，熙寧間，通事舍人十三員。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Hu Shunzhi memorialized: "The Gate office was valued by the founding ancestors: proclamation aides were no more than three to five; in the Xining era, liaison attendants were thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Hu Shunzhi memorialized: "The Gate office was valued by the founding ancestors: proclamation aides were no more than three to five; in the Xining era, liaison attendants were thirteen.

sentences.zh: 祗候六人，當時議者猶以為多。

translations.literal: Attendants six—commentators at the time still thought that many.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants numbered six, and commentators at the time still thought that many.

sentences.zh: 今舍人一百八員，祗候七十六員，看班四員，內免職者二百三員，由宦侍恩幸以求財，朱勔父子賣尤多，富商豪子往往得之。

translations.literal: Now aides number 108, attendants 76, formation-viewers 4, and among them 203 are excused from duty; through eunuch favor they seek wealth, Zhu Mian father and son sold the most posts, and rich merchants and powerful sons often obtained them.
translations.idiomatic: Now there are 108 aides, 76 attendants, and 4 formation-viewers, and among them 203 are excused from duty; through eunuch favor they seek wealth, Zhu Mian and his son sold the most posts, and rich merchants and powerful sons often obtained them.

sentences.zh: 真宗時，諸王夫人因聖節乞補閤門，帝曰：『此職非可以恩澤授。』

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhenzong's time, imperial princes' consorts asked on a sacred festival to fill Gate posts; the emperor said: "This office cannot be granted by favor."
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Zhenzong's time, imperial princes' consorts asked on a sacred festival to fill Gate posts; the emperor said: "This office cannot be granted by favor."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位之初，用宮邸直省官郭昭選為閤門祗候，司馬光言：『此祖宗以蓄養賢才，在文臣為館職。』

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shenzong's accession, palace-residence direct-provincial official Guo Zhaoxuan was appointed Gate attendant; Sima Guang said: "The ancestors used this to cultivate talent; for civil officials it is a Hall post."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Shenzong's accession, palace-residence direct-provincial official Guo Zhaoxuan was appointed Gate attendant; Sima Guang said: "The ancestors used this to cultivate talent; for civil officials it is a Hall post."

sentences.zh: 其重如此，今豈可賣以求財，乞賜裁省。」

translations.literal: It was valued thus; how can it now be sold for wealth? I beg that it be cut back."
translations.idiomatic: It was valued thus; how can it now be sold for wealth? I beg that it be cut back."

sentences.zh: 故有是詔。

translations.literal: Therefore there was this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore there was this edict.

sentences.zh: 舊制有東、西上閤門，多以處外戚勳貴。

translations.literal: Under the old system there were Eastern and Western Upper Gates, mostly used to place imperial affines and meritorious nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system there were Eastern and Western Upper Gates, mostly reserved for imperial affines and meritorious nobles.

sentences.zh: 建炎初元，並省爲一，其引進司、四方館並歸閤門，客省循舊法，非橫行不許知閤門。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan they were merged into one; the Introduction Bureau and Four Directions Hostel were both returned to the Gate office, the Reception Bureau followed the old law, and only transverse-rank officers were permitted to hold Gate office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyan the two gates were merged; the Introduction Bureau and Four Directions Hostel were placed under the Gate office, the Reception Bureau followed the old rules, and only transverse-rank officers could hold Gate office.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，帝以宋篯孫藩邸舊人，稍習儀注，命轉行橫行一官，主管閤門。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, because Song Biansun was an old man of the princely residence and somewhat versed in ritual regulations, the emperor ordered him to advance one transverse-rank step and supervise the Gate office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 the emperor, finding Song Biansun an old retainer of the princely residence with some knowledge of court ritual, advanced him one transverse rank and put him in charge of the Gate office.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「藩邸舊人，自内侍及使臣皆不與行在職任，止與外任，篯孫以閤門無諳練人，故留之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Old men of the princely residence, from inner attendants to envoys, are not given posts at the traveling court, only outer appointments; Biansun is kept because the Gate office lacks practiced men."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Old retainers of the princely residence, whether inner attendants or envoys, are not given posts at the traveling court, only outer appointments; Biansun is kept because the Gate office lacks practiced men."

sentences.zh: 五年，詔右武大夫以上並稱知閤門事兼客省、四方館事，官未至者，卽稱同知閤門事同兼客省、四方館事，以除授爲序，稱同知者在知閤門之下。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict said that Right Martial Grandee and above were all styled Manager of Gate Affairs concurrently holding Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel affairs; if rank had not yet been reached, they were styled Associate Manager of Gate Affairs with the same concurrent duties, ordered by appointment sequence, with associates ranking below managers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1135 an edict styled Right Martial Grandee and above as Manager of Gate Affairs with concurrent Reception Bureau and Four Directions Hostel duties; men below that rank were Associate Managers with the same concurrent duties, ordered by appointment sequence below the managers.

sentences.zh: 宣讚舍人任傳宣引讚之事，與閤門祗候並爲閤職，間帶點檢閤門薄書公事。

translations.literal: Proclamation aides handled proclamation and leading duties, and together with Gate attendants formed Gate posts, sometimes also checking Gate registry business.
translations.idiomatic: Proclamation aides handled proclamation and leading duties; together with Gate attendants they formed Gate posts and sometimes also checked Gate registry business.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，許令供職，注授内外合入差遣，闕到然後免供職。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era, service in office was permitted; suitable inner and outer appointments were registered, and only when a vacancy was filled was service ended.
