translations.idiomatic: During Shaoxing, officers were allowed to serve in office while registered for suitable inner or outer appointments and released only when a vacancy was filled.

sentences.zh: 其後供職舍人員數稍冗，裁定以四十員爲額。

translations.literal: Later the number of serving aides became somewhat excessive, and a quota of forty was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the number of serving aides grew excessive, and a quota of forty was fixed.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，上欲清閤門之選，除宣讚舍人、閤門祗候仍舊通掌讚引之職外，置閤門舍人十員，以待武舉之入官者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao, the emperor wished to clarify Gate selection; apart from proclamation aides and Gate attendants still jointly managing proclamation and leading duties, ten Gate aides were established to await those entering office through the military examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiandao, the emperor wished to clarify Gate selection; apart from proclamation aides and Gate attendants still jointly managing proclamation and leading duties, ten Gate aides were established to await those entering office through the military examination.

sentences.zh: 掌諸殿覺察失儀兼侍立，駕出行幸亦如之。

translations.literal: They observed breaches of ritual in all halls and also attended standing by, and likewise on imperial outings and visits.
translations.idiomatic: They observed breaches of ritual in all halls and also attended standing by, and likewise on imperial outings and visits.

sentences.zh: 六參、常朝，後殿引親王起居。

translations.literal: At six audiences and regular court, they led imperial princes' attendance in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: At six audiences and regular court, they led imperial princes' attendance in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 仿儒臣館閣之制，召試中書省，然後命之。

translations.literal: Following the system for civil officials' Hall and Pavilion posts, they were summoned for examination at the Secretariat and then appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Following the system for civil officials' Hall and Pavilion posts, they were summoned for examination at the Secretariat and then appointed.

sentences.zh: 又許轉對如職事官，供職滿三年與邊郡。

translations.literal: They were also permitted to present memorials in audience like regular officials; after three years of service they were given border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: They were also permitted to present memorials in audience like regular officials; after three years of service they were given border prefectures.

sentences.zh: 淳熙間，置看班祗候，令忠訓郎以下充，秉義郎以上，始除閤門祗候。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era, formation-viewing attendants were established, filled from Loyal Instruction Gentleman downward; from Upholding Righteousness Gentleman upward, one was first appointed Gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunxi era, formation-viewing attendants were established, filled from Loyal Instruction Gentleman downward; from Upholding Righteousness Gentleman upward, one was first appointed Gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 又增重薦舉閤門祗候之制，必廉幹有方略、善弓馬、兩任親民無遺闕及曾曆邊任者充。

translations.literal: The system for recommending Gate attendants was also strengthened: appointees had to be incorrupt and capable with strategy, skilled in bow and horse, without omissions in two terms of close service to the people, or have served on the border.
translations.idiomatic: The system for recommending Gate attendants was also strengthened: appointees had to be incorrupt and capable with strategy, skilled in bow and horse, without omissions in two terms of close service to the people, or have served on the border.

sentences.zh: 紹熙以來，立定員額。

translations.literal: From Shaoxi onward, fixed quotas were established.
translations.idiomatic: From Shaoxi onward, fixed quotas were established.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，申嚴合門長官選擇其屬之令，非右科前名之士不預召試，蓋以爲右列淸選云。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan, the order was strictly proclaimed that Gate chiefs select their subordinates; only those who had ranked at the top of the military examination were summoned for testing—it was regarded as a clear selection among the military ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qingyuan, the order was strictly proclaimed that Gate chiefs select their subordinates; only those who had ranked at the top of the military examination were summoned for testing—it was regarded as a clear selection among the military ranks.

sentences.zh: 【帶御器械】宋初，選三班以上武幹親信者佩櫜鞬、御劒，或以内臣爲之，止名：御帶」。

translations.literal: Bearer of Imperial Arms: In early Song, trusted military officers of third rank and above were selected to wear sword scabbards and imperial swords, or inner attendants were appointed; the title was simply Imperial Bearer."
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of Imperial Arms: In early Song, trusted military officers of third rank and above wore sword scabbards and imperial swords, or inner attendants were appointed; the title was simply Imperial Bearer."

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，改爲帶御器械。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, it was changed to Bearer of Imperial Arms.
translations.idiomatic: In 998 it was renamed Bearer of Imperial Arms.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，詔自今無得過六人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, an edict said that from now on the number must not exceed six.
translations.idiomatic: In 1035 an edict capped the post at six officers.

sentences.zh: 慶暦元年，詔遇闕員，曾暦邊任有功者補之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingli, an edict said that when vacancies occurred, those who had served on the border with merit should fill them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1041 vacancies were to be filled by men with meritorious border service.

sentences.zh: 中興初，諸將在外多帶職，蓋假禁近之名，爲軍旅之重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the restoration, generals abroad often carried the title concurrently, borrowing the name of close palace service to lend weight to military command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the restoration, field generals often held the title concurrently, borrowing palace proximity to lend weight to military command.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，樞密院言：「帶御器械官當帶插。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Bearers of Imperial Arms should wear insertion knives."
translations.idiomatic: In 1137 the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Bearers of Imperial Arms should wear insertion knives."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此官本以衞不虞，今乃佩數笴骹箭，不知何用。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This office was originally to guard against the unexpected; now they wear several bundles of socketed arrows—what use is that?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This office was meant to guard against the unexpected, yet now they wear bundles of socketed arrows to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 方承平時，至飾以珠玉，車駕毎出，爲觀美而已。

translations.literal: In peaceful times they are even adorned with pearls and jade, and whenever the imperial carriage goes out it is only for display.
translations.idiomatic: In peaceful times they are even adorned with pearls and jade whenever the imperial carriage goes out, purely for display.

sentences.zh: 他日恢復，此等事當盡去之。」

translations.literal: When the realm is restored one day, such things should all be removed."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is restored, such things should all be abolished."

sentences.zh: 二十九年，詔中外舉薦武臣，無闕可處，增置帶御器械四員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, an edict recommended military officers throughout the empire; with no vacancies to place them in, four additional Bearers of Imperial Arms were established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1159, when recommended military officers had no vacancies, four additional Bearers of Imperial Arms were created.

sentences.zh: 然近侍亦或得之。

translations.literal: Yet close attendants sometimes received the title as well.
translations.idiomatic: Close attendants sometimes received the title as well.

sentences.zh: 乾道發來，詔立班樞密院檢詳文之上。

translations.literal: When Qiandao began, an edict ordered them to stand in formation above the document examiners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Qiandao, an edict placed them in formation above the Bureau of Military Affairs document examiners.

sentences.zh: 淳熙間，凡正除軍中差遣或外任者，不許銜内帶行，又須供職一年，方與解帶恩例，於是屬之職益加重焉。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era, those formally appointed to military assignments in the capital or to outer posts were not permitted to carry the inner title concurrently; they also had to serve one year before receiving the favor of removing the title—thus the weight of the office increased further.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi, men formally appointed to capital military assignments or outer posts could not carry the inner title concurrently and had to serve one year before the favor of removing it—making the office still more weighty.

sentences.zh: 【入內內侍省 內侍省】宋初，有内中髙品班院，淳化五年，改入内内班院，又改入内黃門班院，又改内侍省入内内侍班院。

translations.literal: Inner-Palace Inner Service and Inner Service: In early Song there was the Inner High-Rank Detachment; in the fifth year of Chunhua it was changed to Inner Inner Detachment, then to Inner Yellow Gate Detachment, then to Inner Service Inner Inner Service Detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-Palace Inner Service and Inner Service: In early Song there was the Inner High-Rank Detachment; in 994 it was changed to Inner Inner Detachment, then to Inner Yellow Gate Detachment, then to Inner Service Inner Inner Service Detachment.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，詔：「東門取索司可並隸内東門司，餘入内都知司；

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, an edict said: "The Eastern Gate Requisition Office may be merged under the Inner Eastern Gate Office; the rest under the Inner Chief Steward Office;
translations.idiomatic: In 1006, an edict said: "The Eastern Gate Requisition Office may be merged under the Inner Eastern Gate Office; the rest under the Inner Chief Steward Office;

sentences.zh: 内東門都知司、内侍省入内内侍班院可立爲入内内侍省，以諸司隸之。」

translations.literal: the Inner Eastern Gate Chief Steward Office and Inner Service Inner Inner Service Detachment may be established as the Inner-Palace Inner Service, with all offices subordinate to it."
translations.idiomatic: the Inner Eastern Gate Chief Steward Office and Inner Service Inner Inner Service Detachment may be established as the Inner-Palace Inner Service, with all offices subordinate to it."

sentences.zh: 宋初，有内班院，淳化五年，改爲黃門，九月，又改内侍省。

translations.literal: In early Song there was the Inner Detachment; in the fifth year of Chunhua it was changed to Yellow Gate; in the ninth month it was changed again to Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: In early Song there was the Inner Detachment; in 994 it was changed to Yellow Gate; in the ninth month it was changed again to Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 入内内侍省與内侍省號爲前後省，而入内省尤爲親近。

translations.literal: The Inner-Palace Inner Service and Inner Service were called the front and rear services, and the inner-palace service was especially close.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner-Palace Inner Service and Inner Service were called the front and rear services, and the inner-palace service was especially close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 通侍禁中、役縣褻近者，隸入内内侍省。

translations.literal: Those who served throughout the forbidden palace and worked in intimate proximity were subordinate to the Inner-Palace Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: Those who served throughout the forbidden palace and worked in intimate proximity were subordinate to the Inner-Palace Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 拱侍殿中、備灑掃之職、役使雜品者，隸内侍省。

translations.literal: Those who attended in the halls, prepared sweeping duties, and served miscellaneous ranks were subordinate to the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: Those who attended in the halls, prepared sweeping duties, and served miscellaneous ranks were subordinate to the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 入内内侍省有都都知，都知，副都知，押班，内東頭供奉官，内西頭供奉官，内侍殿頭，内侍髙品，内侍髙班，内侍黄門。

translations.literal: The Inner-Palace Inner Service had chief-of-chiefs steward, chief steward, vice chief steward, escort shift leader, inner eastern tribute officer, inner western tribute officer, inner service hall head, inner service high rank, inner service high shift, and inner service yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner-Palace Inner Service had chief-of-chiefs steward, chief steward, vice chief steward, escort shift leader, inner eastern tribute officer, inner western tribute officer, inner service hall head, inner service high rank, inner service high shift, and inner service yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 内侍省有左班都知、副都知，右班都知、副都知，押班，内東頭供奉官，内西頭供奉官，内侍殿頭，内侍髙品，内侍髙班，内侍黄門。

translations.literal: The Inner Service had left-shift chief steward, vice chief steward, right-shift chief steward, vice chief steward, escort shift leader, inner eastern tribute officer, inner western tribute officer, inner service hall head, inner service high rank, inner service high shift, and inner service yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Service had left-shift chief steward, vice chief steward, right-shift chief steward, vice chief steward, escort shift leader, inner eastern tribute officer, inner western tribute officer, inner service hall head, inner service high rank, inner service high shift, and inner service yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 自供奉官至黄門以二百八十人爲定員。

translations.literal: From tribute officers to yellow gate, the fixed quota was 280 persons.
translations.idiomatic: From tribute officers to yellow gate, the fixed quota was 280 persons.

sentences.zh: 凡内侍初補曰小黃門，經恩遷補則爲内侍黃門。

translations.literal: All inner attendants on first appointment were called junior yellow gate; after grace transfer they became inner service yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: All inner attendants on first appointment were called junior yellow gate; after grace transfer they became inner service yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 後省官闕，則以前省官補。

translations.literal: When rear-service posts were vacant, front-service officers filled them.
translations.idiomatic: When rear-service posts were vacant, front-service officers filled them.

sentences.zh: 押班次遷副都知，次遷都都知，遂為內臣之極品。

translations.literal: From escort shift leader one advanced to vice chief steward, then to chief-of-chiefs steward, thus reaching the highest rank among inner officials.
translations.idiomatic: From escort shift leader one advanced to vice chief steward, then to chief-of-chiefs steward, thus reaching the highest rank among inner officials.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，入內內侍省內侍省都知、押班遂省，各以轉入先後相壓，永為定式。

translations.literal: In the Xining era, the chief stewards and escort shift leaders of the Inner-Palace Inner Service and Inner Service were reduced; each advanced according to order of transfer, pressing by seniority, permanently as the fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xining era, the chief stewards and escort shift leaders of the Inner-Palace Inner Service and Inner Service were reduced; each advanced according to order of transfer, pressing by seniority, permanently as the fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 其官稱，則有內客省使、延福宮使、宣政使、宣慶使、昭宣使。

translations.literal: Their titles included Inner Reception Commissioner, Yanfu Palace Commissioner, Xuanzheng Commissioner, Xuanqing Commissioner, and Zhaoxuan Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Their titles included Inner Reception Commissioner, Yanfu Palace Commissioner, Xuanzheng Commissioner, Xuanqing Commissioner, and Zhaoxuan Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元豐議改官制，張誠一欲易都知、押班之名，置殿中監以易內侍省。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng reform of the rank system was discussed, Zhang Chengyi wished to change the names of chief steward and escort shift leader and establish a Palace Directorate to replace the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng reform of the rank system was discussed, Zhang Chengyi wished to change the names of chief steward and escort shift leader and establish a Palace Directorate to replace the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 既而宰執進呈，神宗曰：「祖宗為此名有深意，豈可輕議？」

translations.literal: When the chief ministers presented this, Emperor Shenzong said: "The ancestors gave these names deep meaning—how can they be lightly discussed?"
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers presented this, Emperor Shenzong said: "The ancestors gave these names deep meaning—how can they be lightly discussed?"

sentences.zh: 政和二年，始遂改焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, the change was finally carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In 1112, the change was finally carried out.

sentences.zh: 以通侍大夫易內客省使，正侍大夫易延福宮使，中侍大夫易景福殿使，中亮大夫易宣慶使，中衛大夫易宣政使，拱衛大夫易昭宣使，供奉官易內東頭供奉官，左侍禁易內西頭供奉官，右侍禁易內侍殿頭，左班殿直易內侍高品，右班殿直易內侍高班，而黃門之名如故。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Grandee replaced Inner Reception Commissioner; Regular Attendant Grandee replaced Yanfu Palace Commissioner; Central Attendant Grandee replaced Jingfu Hall Commissioner; Central Bright Grandee replaced Xuanqing Commissioner; Central Guard Grandee replaced Xuanzheng Commissioner; Arch Guard Grandee replaced Zhaoxuan Commissioner; tribute officer replaced inner eastern tribute officer; left attendant forbidden replaced inner western tribute officer; right attendant forbidden replaced inner service hall head; left-shift palace direct replaced inner service high rank; right-shift palace direct replaced inner service high shift; the name yellow gate remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Grandee replaced Inner Reception Commissioner; Regular Attendant Grandee replaced Yanfu Palace Commissioner; Central Attendant Grandee replaced Jingfu Hall Commissioner; Central Bright Grandee replaced Xuanqing Commissioner; Central Guard Grandee replaced Xuanzheng Commissioner; Arch Guard Grandee replaced Zhaoxuan Commissioner; tribute officer replaced inner eastern tribute officer; left attendant forbidden replaced inner western tribute officer; right attendant forbidden replaced inner service hall head; left-shift palace direct replaced inner service high rank; right-shift palace direct replaced inner service high shift; the name yellow gate remained as before.

sentences.zh: 其屬有：禦藥院，勾當官四人，以入內內侍充，掌按驗方書，修合藥劑，以待進禦及供奉禁中之用。

translations.literal: Its subordinates included: Imperial Pharmacy, four acting officers filled by inner-palace inner attendants, managing verification of formulary books, compounding medicines, to await presentation to the throne and service to the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinates included the Imperial Pharmacy, with four acting officers filled by inner-palace inner attendants, managing verification of formulary books, compounding medicines, to await presentation to the throne and service to the forbidden palace.

sentences.zh: 內東門司勾，當官四人，以入內內侍充，掌宮禁人物出入，周知其名數而譏察之。

translations.literal: Inner Eastern Gate Office: four acting officers filled by inner-palace inner attendants, managing entry and exit of persons in the palace forbidden zone, fully knowing their names and numbers and investigating them.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Eastern Gate Office: four acting officers filled by inner-palace inner attendants, managing entry and exit of persons in the palace forbidden zone, fully knowing their names and numbers and investigating them.

sentences.zh: 合同憑由司，監官二人，掌禁中宣索之物，給其要驗，凡特旨賜予，皆具名數憑由，付有司淮給。

translations.literal: Joint Credentials Office: two supervising officers, managing items requisitioned in the forbidden palace, issuing required verification; for all special-grant bestowals, names and numbers were listed on credentials and handed to the responsible offices for authorized distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Joint Credentials Office: two supervising officers, managing items requisitioned in the forbidden palace, issuing required verification; for all special-grant bestowals, names and numbers were listed on credentials and handed to the responsible offices for authorized distribution.

sentences.zh: 管勾往來國信所，管勾官二人，以都知、押班充，掌契丹使介交聘之事。

translations.literal: Overseer of the State Envoy Exchange Office: two overseer officers filled by chief stewards and escort shift leaders, managing Khitan envoy exchange and diplomatic missions.
translations.idiomatic: Overseer of the State Envoy Exchange Office: two overseer officers filled by chief stewards and escort shift leaders, managing Khitan envoy exchange and diplomatic missions.

sentences.zh: 後苑勾當官，無定員，以內侍充，掌苑囿、池沼、台殿種藝雜飾，以備遊幸。

translations.literal: Rear Garden acting officers, no fixed quota, filled by inner attendants, managing gardens, ponds, terraces, planting, and miscellaneous ornament for imperial excursions.
translations.idiomatic: Rear Garden acting officers, with no fixed quota, filled by inner attendants, managing gardens, ponds, terraces, planting, and miscellaneous ornament for imperial excursions.

sentences.zh: 造作所，掌造作禁中及皇屬婚娶之名物。

translations.literal: Manufacturing Office: managed manufacture of named items for the forbidden palace and imperial-clan weddings.
translations.idiomatic: Manufacturing Office: managed manufacture of named items for the forbidden palace and imperial-clan weddings.

sentences.zh: 龍圖、無章、寶文閣，勾當四人，以入內內侍充，掌藏祖宗文章、圖籍及符瑞寶玩之物，而安像設以崇奉之。

translations.literal: Dragon Diagram, Unmarked, and Treasured Literature Pavilions: four acting officers filled by inner-palace inner attendants, storing the ancestors' writings, maps and books, and talismanic treasures and curios, and arranging image settings to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Diagram, Unmarked, and Treasured Literature Pavilions: four acting officers filled by inner-palace inner attendants, storing the ancestors' writings, maps and books, and talismanic treasures and curios, and arranging image settings to honor them.

sentences.zh: 軍頭引見司，勾當官五人，以內侍省都知、押班及合門宣讚舍人以上充，掌供奉便殿禁衛諸軍入見之事，及馬，步兩直軍員之名。

translations.literal: Army Head Presentation Office: five acting officers filled by Inner Service chief stewards, escort shift leaders, and Gate proclamation aides and above, managing presentation of forbidden-guard armies entering audience in the convenience hall, and the registers of cavalry and infantry direct unit personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Army Head Presentation Office: five acting officers filled by Inner Service chief stewards, escort shift leaders, and Gate proclamation aides and above, managing presentation of forbidden-guard armies entering audience in the convenience hall, and the registers of cavalry and infantry direct unit personnel.

sentences.zh: 翰林院，勾當官一員，以內侍押班、都知充，總天文、書藝、圖畫、醫官四局，凡執伎以事上者皆在焉。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy: one acting officer, filled by Inner Service escort shift leaders and chief stewards, overseeing the four bureaus of astronomy, literary arts, painting, and medical officers; all who practice skills in service to the sovereign were therein.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academy had one acting officer, appointed from Inner Service escort shift leaders and chief stewards, who oversaw the astronomy, literary arts, painting, and medical bureaus; everyone who practiced an art in service to the throne belonged to it.

sentences.zh: 中興以來，深懲內侍用事之弊，嚴前後省使臣與兵將官往來之禁，著內侍官不許出謁及接見賓客之令。

translations.literal: Since the Restoration, the abuse of eunuchs wielding power was deeply punished; strict prohibitions were placed on exchange between front and rear Office commissioners and military officers; regulations were issued that eunuch officials might not go out paying calls or receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty's restoration, the court sharply curbed eunuch power, forbade exchanges between inner and outer court commissioners and military officers, and ordered that eunuch officials could neither pay calls outside nor receive guests.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十年，詔內侍省所掌職務不多，徒有冗費，可廢並歸入內內侍省。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing, an edict said the duties managed by the Inner Service were few and merely produced redundant expense; it could be abolished and merged into the Inner Palace Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: In 1160, an edict declared that the Inner Service handled few duties at wasteful cost and should be abolished and absorbed into the Inner Palace Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 舊制，內侍遇聖節許進子，年十二試以墨義，即中程者，候三年引見供職。

translations.literal: Under the old system, on sacred festivals eunuchs were permitted to present sons; at age twelve they were tested on ink-meaning essays, and those who immediately met the standard waited three years for presentation and appointment to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, eunuchs could present sons on imperial festivals; at twelve the boys took a written examination, and those who passed at once waited three years before being presented and assigned to service.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，殿中侍御史張震言宦者員眾，孝宗即命內侍省具見在人數，免會慶節進子，仍定以二百人為額。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, Palace Secretariat investigating censor Zhang Zhen said eunuchs were too numerous; Xiaozong immediately ordered the Inner Service to list those presently on the rolls, exempted presentation of sons at the Assembly Celebration festival, and fixed the quota at two hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1162, investigating censor Zhang Zhen warned that eunuchs had grown too numerous; Xiaozong at once ordered a head count, ended the practice of presenting sons at the Assembly Celebration festival, and capped the corps at two hundred.

sentences.zh: 乾道間，以差赴德壽宮應奉闕人，增置二百五十人。

translations.literal: During Qiandao, because those dispatched to serve the Deshou Palace were insufficient, the quota was increased to two hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiandao era, vacancies for attendants at the Deshou Palace led to an increase of the eunuch quota to two hundred fifty.

sentences.zh: 紹熙三年，依宰臣奏，中官隻令承受宮禁中事，不許預聞他事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxi, per the chief ministers' memorial, palace eunuchs were only to receive affairs within the palace boundaries and were not permitted to hear of other matters.
translations.idiomatic: In 1192, on the chief ministers' advice, palace eunuchs were restricted to palace affairs alone and barred from involvement elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 嘉定初，詔內侍省陳乞恩例，親屬充寄班祗候，以十年為限。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiading, an edict said that when the Inner Service petitioned for favors, relatives might fill relay-shift attendant posts for a limit of ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiading reign, an edict allowed Inner Service petitions for favors to place relatives in relay-shift attendant posts for no more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 【開封府】牧、尹不常置，權知府一人，以待制以上充。

translations.literal: Kaifeng Prefecture: the Intendant and Prefect were not regularly established; one acting prefectural commissioner was appointed, filled from Assistant Gentleman for Drafting and above.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng Prefecture: Intendant and Prefect were not standing posts; a single acting prefect, drawn from officials of drafting-assistant rank or higher, held the office.

sentences.zh: 掌尹正畿甸之事，以教法導民而勸課之。

translations.literal: He managed metropolitan rectification of the royal domain, guided the people through teaching law, and encouraged taxation.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the capital region, instructed the people through law, and urged payment of taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 中都之獄訟皆受而聽焉，小事則專決，大事則稟奏。

translations.literal: All lawsuits of the capital were received and heard; minor matters were decided on his own authority, major ones reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect took every lawsuit in the capital: minor cases he decided himself, major ones he reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 若承旨已斷者，刑部、御史臺無輒糾察。

translations.literal: If already decided by imperial instruction, the Ministry of Justice and the Censorate might not lightly scrutinize.
translations.idiomatic: Cases already settled by imperial order could not be second-guessed by the Ministry of Justice or the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 屏除寇盜，有奸伏則戒所隸官捕治。

translations.literal: Bandits and robbers were cleared away; when treachery lurked, subordinate officials were warned to arrest and punish.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed brigandage, and when hidden criminals appeared he ordered subordinates to seize and punish them.

sentences.zh: 凡戶口、賦役、道釋之占京邑者，頒其禁令，會其帳籍。

translations.literal: For all household registers, taxes and corvée, and Daoist and Buddhist residency in the capital district, he issued prohibitions and reconciled the registers.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated households, taxes, corvée, and Buddhist and Daoist residents in the capital, issuing bans and keeping the registers in order.

sentences.zh: 大禮，橋道頓遞則為之使，仗內奉引則差官攝牧。

translations.literal: At grand rites he served as envoy for bridges, roads, and relay stations; when leading within the guard formation he dispatched officials to act as Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: On great state ceremonies he arranged bridges, roads, and courier relays; inside the imperial guard he sent deputies to stand in as metropolitan intendant.

sentences.zh: 其屬有判官、推官四人，日視推鞫，分事以治。

translations.literal: Subordinates included four judges and investigating officers who daily oversaw interrogation and divided affairs to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Four judges and investigating officers assisted him, examining cases each day and dividing the workload.

sentences.zh: 而佐其長，領南司者一人，督察使院，非刑獄訟訴則主行之。

translations.literal: Assisting the chief, one person led the Southern Office, supervised the envoy courtyard, and unless the matter concerned criminal detention or lawsuits, directed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: One aide assisted the prefect, heading the Southern Office and supervising the envoy court; except for criminal detention and litigation, he ran routine business.

sentences.zh: 司錄參軍一人，折戶婚之訟，而通書六曹之案牒。

translations.literal: One Registrar Assistant settled household and marriage suits and communicated the case dossiers of the six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: A registrar assistant heard household and marriage disputes and routed paperwork among the six bureaus.

sentences.zh: 功曹、倉曹、戶曹、兵曹、法曹、士曹參軍各一人，視其官曹分職蒞事。

translations.literal: One Merit, Granary, Household, Military, Law, and Gentlemen Bureau Assistant each attended affairs according to the division of duties in his bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the six bureaus—Merit, Granary, Household, Military, Law, and Gentlemen—had one assistant who handled its portfolio.

sentences.zh: 左右軍巡使、判官各二人，分掌京城爭鬥及推鞫之事。

translations.literal: Left and right Military Patrol commissioners and judges, two each, divided management of capital brawls and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Two military patrol commissioners and two judges on each flank handled street fights and interrogations in the capital.

sentences.zh: 左右廂公事幹當官四人，掌檢覆推問，凡鬥訟事輕者聽論決。

translations.literal: Four left and right ward public affairs acting officers managed review and interrogation; for light brawl suits they were permitted to render settlement judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Four ward acting officers on the left and right reviewed cases; in minor brawls they could settle disputes themselves.

sentences.zh: 領縣十有八，鎮二十有四，令佐、訓練、征榷、監臨、巡警之官，知府事者率統隸焉。

translations.literal: It led eighteen counties and twenty-four towns; magistrates, assistants, training officers, tax collectors, supervisors, and patrol officers were all generally commanded by whoever held prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen counties and twenty-four towns fell under its jurisdiction, with magistrates, assistants, drill officers, tax agents, supervisors, and patrolmen all under the prefect's overall command.

sentences.zh: 分案六，置吏六百。

translations.literal: Six case divisions were established, with six hundred clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The office ran six divisions and employed six hundred clerks.

sentences.zh: 開封典司轂下，自建隆以來，為要劇之任。

translations.literal: Kaifeng governed the area under the capital hub; since Jianlong it had been a critical post.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng administered the metropolitan core and, since the Jianlong founding, ranked among the empire's most demanding posts.

sentences.zh: 至熙寧間，增給吏錄，禁其受賕，省衙前役以寬民力，厘折獄訟歸於廂官，而治事視前日損去十四。

translations.literal: By the Xining era, clerk registers were increased, bribes were forbidden, office-front corvée was reduced to ease the people, brawl lawsuits were returned to ward officers, and cases handled daily were fourteen fewer than before.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong's Xining reforms the prefecture expanded clerk rolls, banned bribes, cut corvée at government gates, sent petty quarrels back to ward officers, and reduced daily caseloads by fourteen.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，詔府界捕盜官吏隸本府，與都大提舉司同管轄而掌其賞罰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, an edict placed capital-district bandit-catching officials under this prefecture, co-administered with the Grand Commissionerate, which controlled rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086, capital-district constables were placed under Kaifeng Prefecture and the Grand Commissionerate, which shared jurisdiction and set rewards and penalties.

sentences.zh: 置新城內左、右二廂。

translations.literal: Inner new-city left and right wards were established.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right wards were created inside the new city wall.

sentences.zh: 三年，以罷大理寺獄，置軍巡院判官一員。

translations.literal: In the third year, because the Court of Judicial Review prison was abolished, one Military Patrol Court judge was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088, after the Court of Judicial Review prison closed, Kaifeng added one military patrol court judge.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷新置二廂。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the newly established two wards were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1089 the two new wards were abolished.

sentences.zh: 六年，王嚴叟言：「左、右廳推官公事詞狀，初無通治明文，請事係朝省及奏請通治外，餘並據號分治。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Wang Yansou said: "The official documents and plaints of the left and right hall investigating officers had no explicit rule for joint handling; apart from matters tied to the court ministries or memorials requiring joint handling, the rest should be divided by case number."
translations.idiomatic: In 1091, Wang Yansou said: "Apart from cases bound for the central ministries or requiring joint memorials, left and right hall investigating officers should divide cases by docket number."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，知府事錢勰言：「自祖宗以來，並分左右廳置推官各一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, acting prefect Qian Kai said: "Since the founding ancestors, left and right halls each had one investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1094, acting prefect Qian Kai said: "Since the founding ancestors, Kaifeng has kept one investigating officer in each hall.

sentences.zh: 近年止除推官，元祐中，並令分治。

translations.literal: In recent years only investigating officers were appointed; in Yuanyou, all were ordered to divide cases.
translations.idiomatic: Recently only investigating officers had been named, and under Yuanyou they were told to split the caseload.

sentences.zh: 請依故事分左右廳，各除推官一員，作兩廳共治職事。」

translations.literal: I request that, per precedent, left and right halls each appoint one investigating officer and that the two halls jointly manage duties."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to restore the old practice of one investigating officer per hall, with both halls sharing the work."

sentences.zh: 又言：「熙寧中，置舊城左右廂，元祐初，增置於新城內，四年，罷增置兩廂，今請復置。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In Xining, old-city left and right wards were established; at the start of Yuanyou additions were made inside the new city; in the fourth year the added two wards were abolished; I now request restoration."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In the Xining era, left and right wards were established in the old city; at the start of Yuanyou additions were made inside the new city; in the fourth year the added two wards were abolished; I now request restoration."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔開封、祥符知縣事自今選秩通判人充。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict said that the county magistracies of Kaifeng and Xiangfu would henceforth be filled by registrar-ranked vice prefects.
translations.idiomatic: In 1096, Kaifeng and Xiangfu counties were to be run by vice prefects of registrar rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔開封府所薦推、判官，並召對取旨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict said that investigating officers and judges recommended by Kaifeng Prefecture were all to be summoned for audience and receive imperial instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1097, every investigating officer and judge the prefecture recommended had to appear before the emperor for appointment.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，蔡京奏：「乞罷權知府，置牧一員、尹一員，專總府事；

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, Cai Jing memorialized: "I request abolishing the acting prefect, establishing one Intendant and one Prefect to oversee all prefectural affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In 1104, Cai Jing memorialized: "I request abolishing the acting prefect, establishing one Intendant and one Prefect to oversee all prefectural affairs;

sentences.zh: 少尹二員，分左右，貳府之政事。

translations.literal: two Junior Prefects, left and right, to assist prefectural administration.
translations.idiomatic: two Junior Prefects, one on each flank, would assist in daily administration.

sentences.zh: 牧以皇子領之。

translations.literal: The Intendant was led by an imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial prince would hold the Intendancy.

sentences.zh: 尹以文臣充，在六曹尚書之下、侍郎之上。

translations.literal: The Prefect was filled by a civil official, ranking below the six ministry directors and above vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: A civil official would serve as Prefect, ranking below ministry directors but above vice directors.

sentences.zh: 少尹在左右司郎官之下、列曹郎官之上。

translations.literal: The Junior Prefect ranked below the Left and Right Office gentlemen and above the various bureau gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Prefects stood below the Left and Right Office directors and above the bureau gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 以士、戶、儀、兵、刑、工為六曹次序，司錄二員，六曹各二員，參軍事八員。

translations.literal: The order of the six bureaus was Gentlemen, Household, Rites, Military, Justice, and Works; there were two registrars, two officers per bureau, and eight staff assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Six bureaus—Gentlemen, Household, Rites, Military, Justice, and Works—each had two officers, with two registrars and eight general assistants besides.

sentences.zh: 開封、祥符兩縣置案仿此。

translations.literal: Kaifeng and Xiangfu counties established divisions following this model.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng and Xiangfu counties organized their offices on the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 易胥吏之稱，略依《唐六典》制度。」

translations.literal: Clerk titles were changed, roughly following the system of the "Tang Six Codes."
translations.idiomatic: Clerical titles were renamed, loosely modeled on the system of the Tang Six Codes."

sentences.zh: 又請移開封府治所於舊尚書省，從之。

translations.literal: He also requested moving the Kaifeng Prefecture seat to the old Ministry compound; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also won approval to move the prefectural yamen into the former Ministry of Personnel compound.

sentences.zh: 〈（太宗、真宗嘗任府尹，自到道後，知府者必帶「權」字，蔡京乃以潛邸之號處臣下，建置曹官以上凡十六員，比舊增要官十一員，）〉

translations.literal: (Emperors Taizong and Zhenzong once served as Prefect; after the reign title Daodao, whoever held the prefecture necessarily bore the word "acting"; Cai Jing then applied princely-residence titles to his subordinates, establishing bureau officials and above—sixteen in all, eleven more key posts than before.)
translations.idiomatic: (Emperors Taizong and Zhenzong had served as metropolitan prefect; after Daodao every appointee had to be "acting prefect"; Cai Jing now draped his men in princely household titles, creating sixteen bureau-level posts—eleven more than the old establishment.)

sentences.zh: 五年，詔開封府屬官參軍待並依舊員額。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict said that Kaifeng subordinate staff assistants should wait according to the old quotas.
translations.idiomatic: In 1105, Kaifeng's subordinate assistants were held to the former staffing limits.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，李孝壽乞增置府學博士一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, Li Xiaoshou requested one additional prefectural school erudite.
translations.idiomatic: In 1107, Li Xiaoshou asked for another doctorate instructor at the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 詔：「開封六職閑劇不同，如士曹之官，唯主到罷批書，而刑、戶事繁，自今凡士之婚田鬥訟皆在士曹，餘曹仿此。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "The six duties of Kaifeng differ in leisure and urgency; Gentlemen Bureau officials only managed arrival-and-departure endorsements, while Justice and Household affairs were numerous; from now all gentlemen's marriage, field, and brawl suits belong in the Gentlemen Bureau; other bureaus follow this pattern."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The six duties of Kaifeng differ in leisure and urgency; Gentlemen Bureau officials only managed arrival-and-departure endorsements, while Justice and Household affairs were numerous; from now all gentlemen's marriage, field, and brawl suits belong in the Gentlemen Bureau; other bureaus follow this pattern."

sentences.zh: 二年，詔皇子領牧，祿令如執政官，又詔天下州郡並依開封府分曹置掾。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict said imperial princes would lead as Intendant with salary like chief ministers; another edict said all prefectures and districts should establish bureau clerks following Kaifeng."
translations.idiomatic: The next year princes serving as Intendant received chief-minister salaries, and every prefecture was told to copy Kaifeng's bureau-clerk system.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，復置開封府學錢糧官一員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, one Kaifeng school funds-and-grain officer was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1112, Kaifeng restored a school finance officer for grain funds.

sentences.zh: 五年，盛章奏：乞依尚書六部置架閣主管官一員。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Sheng Zhang memorialized, requesting one archive supervisor following the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1115, Sheng Zhang asked for an archive chief modeled on the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，聶山奏：司錄、六曹官乞依省部少監封敘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, Nie Shan memorialized that registrar and six bureau officials should receive ranking like provincial junior directors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1119, Nie Shan proposed that registrars and six-bureau officers receive the same promotion titles as junior directors in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 詔修入條令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered this revised into the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the rule written into statute.

sentences.zh: 【監安府】舊為杭州，領浙西兵馬鈴轄，建炎三年，詔改為臨安府，其守臣令帶浙西同安撫使。

translations.literal: Lin'an Prefecture: formerly Hangzhou, it led the Western Zhejiang military command; in the third year of Jianyan an edict renamed it Lin'an Prefecture, and its prefect was ordered to bear the concurrent title Western Zhejiang Co-Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an Prefecture had been Hangzhou and commanded Western Zhejiang troops; in 1129 it was renamed Lin'an, and its prefect also served as Western Zhejiang co-pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時置帥在鎮江府，紹興駐驆安遂正稱安撫使置知府一員、通判二員，簽書節度判官廳公事、節度推官、觀察推官、觀察判官、錄事參軍、左司理參軍、右司理參軍、司戶參軍、司法參軍各一員。

translations.literal: At that time the commander was posted at Zhenjiang Prefecture; after the court settled at Lin'an in Shaoxing the title Pacification Commissioner was regularized; there were one prefect, two vice prefects, and one each of secretariat commissioner for military affairs, military investigating officer, observation investigating officer, observation judge, recorder assistant, left judicial assistant, right judicial assistant, household assistant, and judicial assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander remained at Zhenjiang until Shaoxing made Lin'an the capital and regularized the pacification commission; the prefecture then had a prefect, two vice prefects, and single posts for secretariat, military, and observation staff, plus recorder, judicial, household, and law assistants.

sentences.zh: 本府掌畿甸之事，籍其戶口，均其賦役，頒其禁令。

translations.literal: This prefecture managed metropolitan domain affairs, registered households, equalized taxes and corvée, and issued prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an handled capital-region administration: household registers, tax and corvée assessments, and the promulgation of local bans.

sentences.zh: 城外內分南北左右廂，各置廂官，以聽民之訟訴。

translations.literal: Outside and inside the city were divided into northern, southern, left, and right wards, each with ward officers to hear popular lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The city inside and out was split into north, south, left, and right wards, each with an officer to hear residents' suits.

sentences.zh: 〈（廂官許奏辟京朝官親民資序人充，後以臣僚言，罷城內兩廂官，惟城外置焉。）〉

translations.literal: (Ward officers were permitted to nominate capital court officials of close-service rank; later, per officials' memorial, the two inner-city ward officers were abolished and only the outer city retained them.)
translations.idiomatic: (Ward officers could nominate capital officials of close-service rank; later, after officials objected, inner-city ward posts were abolished and only outer wards kept officers.)

sentences.zh: 分使臣十員，以緝捕在城盜賊。

translations.literal: Ten dispatched envoys were assigned to arrest thieves within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ten imperial envoys were detailed to hunt down urban bandits.

sentences.zh: 立五酒務，置監官以裕財。

translations.literal: Five wine monopolies were established, with supervising officers to enrich revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Five government wine offices, each with a supervisor, were set up to swell the treasury.

sentences.zh: 分六都監界分，差兵一百四十八鋪以巡防煙火。

translations.literal: Six metropolitan patrol districts were divided, and troops at one hundred forty-eight posts patrolled against fire.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was divided into six patrol zones, with soldiers at 148 fire-watch posts.

sentences.zh: 置兩總轄，承受御前朝旨文字。

translations.literal: Two grand coordinators were established to receive imperial memorial text from the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief coordinators received memorials bearing the emperor's personal instructions.

sentences.zh: 凡禦寶、禦批、實封有所取索，則供進；

translations.literal: Whenever imperial seals, imperial endorsements, or sealed packets were sought, they were supplied;
translations.idiomatic: When the palace needed imperial seals, endorsements, or sealed packets, the coordinators furnished them;

sentences.zh: 凡省，台、寺、監、監司符牒及管下諸縣及倉場等申到公事，則受而理之；

translations.literal: whenever documents from provinces, terraces, temples, bureaus, supervisory agencies, and reports from subordinate counties and granaries arrived, they were received and handled;
translations.idiomatic: they also received and processed paperwork from ministries, courts, temples, bureaus, commissions, and subordinate counties and granaries;

sentences.zh: 凡大禮及國信，隨事應辦，祠祭共其禮料，會聚陳其幄帟，人使往來，辨其舟楫，皆先期飭於有司。

translations.literal: at grand rites and state letters they responded as needed; for sacrifices they shared ritual goods; for gatherings they arranged banners; for envoys they arranged boats—all prepared beforehand with the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: for state ceremonies and diplomatic letters they made advance arrangements with the proper agencies, supplying ritual goods, ceremonial hangings, and boats for foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 領縣九，分士、戶、儀、兵、刑、工六案。

translations.literal: It led nine counties and divided affairs among six bureaus: Gentlemen, Household, Rites, Military, Justice, and Works.
translations.idiomatic: Nine counties reported to the prefecture, whose work ran through six bureaus—Gentlemen, Household, Rites, Military, Justice, and Works.

sentences.zh: 內戶案分上、中、下案，外有免役案、常平案、上下開拆司、財賦司、大禮局、國信司、排辦司、修造司，各治其事。

translations.literal: The Household Bureau was divided into upper, middle, and lower sections; outside these were the Exemption Corvée Bureau, Ever-Normal Bureau, upper and lower opening offices, Revenue Bureau, Grand Rite Bureau, State Letter Bureau, Arrangement Bureau, and Repair Bureau, each managing its own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Household affairs split into upper, middle, and lower desks, alongside separate offices for corvée exemption, ever-normal granaries, mail opening, revenue, grand rites, diplomatic letters, logistics, and construction—each with its own staff.

sentences.zh: 置吏：點檢文字、都孔目官、副孔目官、節度孔目官、觀察孔目官各一名，磨勘司主押官、正開拆官、副開拆官各一人，下名開拆官二名，押司官八人，前後行守分二十一人，貼司三十人。

translations.literal: Clerks established were: one text checker, one chief clerk, one deputy chief clerk, one military commissioner clerk, one observation commissioner clerk, one auditing chief, one chief opening officer, one deputy opening officer, two lower opening officers, eight registry officers, twenty-one front and rear clerks on fixed shifts, and thirty copyists.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included a document examiner, chief and deputy chief clerks, military and observation clerks, an auditing chief, opening and registry officers, twenty-one shift clerks, and thirty copyists.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，皇太子領尹事，廢臨安府通判、簽判職官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qiandao, the Crown Prince held Prefect duties and the Lin'an vice prefect and signing judge posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1171 the crown prince took the metropolitan prefecture and Lin'an abolished its vice prefect and signing judge.

sentences.zh: 置少尹一員，日受民詞以白太子，間日率僚屬詣宮稟事。

translations.literal: One Junior Prefect was established; daily he received popular petitions to report to the Crown Prince, and every other day he led subordinates to the palace to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A Junior Prefect heard petitions each day and relayed them to the crown prince, leading the staff to the palace on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 置判官二員、推官三員。

translations.literal: Two judges and three investigating officers were established.
translations.idiomatic: Two judges and three investigating officers were added.

sentences.zh: 有旨，少伊比仿知府，判官比通判，推官比幕職官，其統臨職分，並照從來條例。

translations.literal: By decree, the Junior Prefect was modeled on the prefect, judges on the vice prefect, and investigating officers on staff officials; their overall command duties followed the former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: An order equated the Junior Prefect to the prefect, judges to vice prefects, and investigating officers to staff aides, with duties unchanged from earlier rules.

sentences.zh: 九年，皇太子解尹事，臨安府知、通、簽判、推判官並依舊置。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Crown Prince relinquished Prefect duties; Lin'an prefect, vice prefect, signing judge, and investigating judges were all restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1173, after the crown prince stepped down, the prefect, vice prefect, signing judge, and investigating judges were reinstated.

sentences.zh: 既據保義郎趙禮之狀：「臨安府依條合置兵馬監押一員。

translations.literal: Based on the petition of Protector of Righteousness Gentleman Zhao Li: "Lin'an Prefecture by regulation should have one military horse supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Based on the petition of Protector of Righteousness Gentleman Zhao Li: "Lin'an Prefecture by regulation should have one military horse supervisor.

sentences.zh: 經任監當四員，初任監當闕一員，昨皇太子領府尹更不差注，今既辭免，乞將宗室添差員闕衣舊。」

translations.literal: Four experienced supervisors were in post and one initial appointment was vacant; when the Crown Prince held the prefecture no appointments were made; now that he has resigned, I beg that the supplemental vacancies for imperial clansmen be filled according to the old rules."
translations.idiomatic: Four seasoned supervisors were serving but one entry post was empty; the crown prince's tenure had frozen appointments; now that he has withdrawn, please fill the clan supplemental slots under the old rules."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年，詔罷備攝官，惟緝捕使臣十二員、聽候差使六員許令辟置。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi, an edict abolished reserve deputies; only twelve arrest envoys and six awaiting-dispatch officers were permitted nomination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1176, reserve deputies were cut; only twelve arrest envoys and six officers awaiting assignment could be nominated.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰四年，詔臨安府添差不厘務總管路鈐二十員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiatai, an edict added twenty non-duty general route controllers at Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1204, Lin'an was allowed twenty supplemental general route controllers without regular duties.

sentences.zh: 州鈐轄、路分都監、副都監二十員。

translations.literal: Twenty prefectural controllers and route branch chief and deputy supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: It also added twenty prefectural controllers and route branch chief and deputy supervisors.

sentences.zh: 正、副將十五員。

translations.literal: Fifteen chief and deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen chief and deputy generals were authorized.

sentences.zh: 安撫司淮備將領十五員，州都監以下十員。

translations.literal: Fifteen Pacification Bureau Huai River reserve commanders, and ten from prefectural chief supervisor downward.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen reserve commanders for the pacification bureau on the Huai, plus ten posts from prefectural chief supervisor downward.

sentences.zh: 共以八十員為額。

translations.literal: The total quota was eighty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Together these posts capped at eighty.

sentences.zh: 尋減總管路鈐五員。

translations.literal: Soon five general route controllers were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Five general route controllers were soon removed.

sentences.zh: 開禧三年，復省罷總管、路分共六員。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaixi, six abolished general route and branch posts were again reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In 1207, six more general route and branch supervisory posts were cut.

sentences.zh: 【河南應天府】牧尹少尹司錄戶曹法曹士曹尹以下掌同開封府，尹闕則置知府事一人，

translations.literal: Henan Prefecture and Yingtian Prefecture: from the Prefect downward, Intendant, Prefect, Junior Prefect, Registrar, Household Bureau, Law Bureau, and Gentlemen Bureau officials managed the same affairs as Kaifeng Prefecture; if the Prefect was vacant, one person holding prefectural affairs was established,
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Yingtian prefectures mirrored Kaifeng's structure from the Prefect down through registrars and household, law, and gentlemen bureaus; when no Prefect served, an acting prefect took charge,

sentences.zh: 〈（以郎中以上充，二品以上曰判府。

translations.literal: (filled from Gentleman Supervisor and above; second rank and above were titled "adjudicate prefecture.")
translations.idiomatic: (filled by a court official of registrar rank or higher; officials of second rank or above were styled "Prefect-adjudicator.")

sentences.zh: 次府及節度州淮此。）〉

translations.literal: (Secondary prefectures and military commission prefectures followed this.)
translations.idiomatic: (Secondary prefectures and military commission capitals followed the same rule.)

sentences.zh: 通判一人，

translations.literal: one vice prefect,
translations.idiomatic: a single vice prefect,

sentences.zh: 〈（以朝官充。）〉

translations.literal: (filled by a court official.)
translations.idiomatic: (filled by a capital court official.)

sentences.zh: 判官、推官各一人，

translations.literal: one judge and one investigating officer each,
translations.idiomatic: one judicial judge and one investigating officer apiece,

sentences.zh: 〈（或以京朝官簽書。）〉

translations.literal: (or appointed by a capital court official with signing authority.)
translations.idiomatic: (or by a capital official holding concurrent signing authority.)

sentences.zh: 使院牙職、左右軍巡悉同開封，而主、典以下差減其數。

translations.literal: Envoy-courtyard gate staff and left and right Military Patrol posts were all the same as Kaifeng, but from chief and clerk downward the numbers were reduced by degree.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy court's gate staff and left and right military patrols matched Kaifeng's setup, but chief clerks and below were staffed at reduced quotas.

sentences.zh: 戶曹通掌府院戶籍、考課、稅賦，法曹專掌讞議，士曹或蔭敘起家，不常置。

translations.literal: The Household Bureau generally managed prefectural household registers, merit review, and tax levies; the Law Bureau exclusively managed case deliberation; the Gentlemen Bureau might enter through inherited privilege and was not always established.
translations.idiomatic: Household affairs covered registers, merit reviews, and taxes; law officers handled case deliberation alone; the Gentlemen Bureau, often filled by inherited privilege, was not a permanent post.

sentences.zh: 〈（諸州府同。

translations.literal: (The same for all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: (The same rule applied to every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至道初，罷司理院，州置司士，取官吏強慢者為，給簿、尉奉。）〉

translations.literal: In early Zhidao, the Judicial Review Office was abolished; prefectures established Court Gentlemen, taking officials who were forceful and overbearing, and granting registrar and assistant salaries.)
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-990s the judicial review office was abolished; prefectures instead appointed a court gentleman drawn from the most forceful local officers, paid at registrar and assistant rates.)

sentences.zh: 助教有特恩而受者，不厘務。

translations.literal: Teaching assistants who received special favor did not handle duties.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching assistants appointed by special favor were excused from regular duties.

sentences.zh: 【次府】牧尹少尹司錄戶曹法曹士曹司理文學助教牧、尹以下所掌並同開封，

translations.literal: Secondary Prefectures: Intendant, Prefect, Junior Prefect, Registrar, Household Bureau, Law Bureau, Gentlemen Bureau, Judicial Review, Erudite, and Teaching Assistant—from Intendant and Prefect downward all managed the same as Kaifeng,
translations.idiomatic: Title: Secondary Prefectures. The Intendant, Prefect, Junior Prefect, registrar, household, law, and gentlemen bureaus, judicial review, erudite, and teaching assistant—from the Intendant down—handled the same duties as Kaifeng,

sentences.zh: 〈（大中祥符八年，以楚王為興元牧，其後又為京兆、江陵牧，自餘無為者。）〉

translations.literal: (In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the King of Chu was made Intendant of Xingyuan; later he was also Intendant of Jingzhao and Jiangling; thereafter none were appointed.)
translations.idiomatic: (In 1015 the King of Chu became Intendant of Xingyuan, later also of Jingzhao and Jiangling; after that no further appointments were made.)

sentences.zh: 尹闕則知府事一人，

translations.literal: If the Prefect post was vacant, one person holding prefectural affairs was established,
translations.idiomatic: When the Prefect's seat was empty, one acting prefect took charge,

sentences.zh: 〈（以朝官及刺史以上或諸司使充。）〉

translations.literal: (filled by a court official of prefect rank or above or by commissioners of various bureaus.)
translations.idiomatic: (filled by a capital official of prefect rank or higher, or by a bureau commissioner.)

sentences.zh: 通判一人，

translations.literal: one vice prefect,
translations.idiomatic: a single vice prefect,

sentences.zh: 〈（以京朝官充。

translations.literal: (filled by a capital court official.
translations.idiomatic: (filled by a capital court official.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，諸州置通判，統治軍、州之政，事得專達，與長吏均禮。

translations.literal: In early Qiande, vice prefects were established in all prefectures to oversee military and prefectural government; affairs could be reported directly, and they received equal ceremony with the chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the early 960s every prefecture gained a vice prefect to oversee military and civil government; he reported directly to court and was treated as the prefect's equal in ceremony.

sentences.zh: 大藩或置兩員。

translations.literal: Great prefectures might have two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Large prefectures could have two.

sentences.zh: 戶少事簡有不置者，正刺史以上州知州，雖小處亦特置。）〉

translations.literal: Where households were few and affairs simple some had none; for prefectures whose prefect held regular governor rank and above, even small posts were specially given one.)
translations.idiomatic: Sparse or quiet districts sometimes had none, but any prefecture whose prefect held regular governor rank—even a small one—was specially given a vice prefect.)

sentences.zh: 使院牙職事並同前。

translations.literal: Envoy-courtyard gate staff duties were the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy court's gate staff followed the same rules as before.

sentences.zh: 【節度使】宋初無所掌，其事務悉歸本州知州、通判兼總之，亦無定員。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner: At the beginning of Song none held authority; all affairs were jointly overseen by the home prefecture's prefect and vice prefect, and there was also no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Title: Military Commissioner. Early in the dynasty the title carried no executive power; the prefect and vice prefect of the home prefecture ran everything, and there was no fixed number of appointees.

sentences.zh: 恩數與執政同。

translations.literal: Favor privileges equaled those of chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Its ceremonial privileges matched those of chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 初除，鎖院降麻，其禮尤異，以待宗室近屬、外戚、國壻年勞久次者。

translations.literal: On first appointment the academy was sealed and hemp was decreed—its ceremony especially unusual—for imperial clansmen of close kin, affinal kin, imperial sons-in-law, and men of long service.
translations.idiomatic: First appointments were sealed in the academy and announced by hemp decree in an especially elaborate ceremony, reserved for close imperial kin, affinal relatives, imperial sons-in-law, and men of long service.

sentences.zh: 若外任，除殿帥始授此官，亦止於一員；

translations.literal: If posted outside, only upon leaving the Palace Commander post was this title first granted, and only to one person;
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital it was first granted only when a palace commander left that post, and only to one man at a time;

sentences.zh: 或有功勳顯著，任帥守於外，及前宰執拜者，尤不輕授。

translations.literal: or if merit was outstanding while holding command outside, or former chief ministers were appointed—it was especially not lightly granted.
translations.idiomatic: men of outstanding merit commanding in the provinces, or former chief ministers, were especially unlikely to receive it casually.

sentences.zh: 又遵唐制，以節度使兼中書令、或侍中、或中書門下平章事，皆謂之使相，以待勳賢故老及宰相久次罷政者；

translations.literal: Following Tang practice, a military commissioner might concurrently hold Zhongshu Ling, Shi Zhong, or Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi—all called commissioner-ministers—for meritorious elders and long-serving dismissed chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Following Tang practice, a military commissioner might also hold Grand Counselor, Palace Attendant, or Grand Councilor—all styled commissioner-ministers—for meritorious elders and long-serving retired chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 隨其舊職或檢校官加節度使出判大藩，通謂之使相。

translations.literal: with his former office or acting title plus military commissioner, he was sent to judge a great prefecture, and was generally called a commissioner-minister.
translations.idiomatic: or, retaining his former or acting rank, he was sent out as military commissioner to govern a major prefecture and was commonly called a commissioner-minister.

sentences.zh: 元豐以新製，始改為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng, under the new regulations, it was first changed to Keeper of the Palace with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanfeng's new regulations the title was first changed to Palace Keeper with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 舊制，敕出中書門下，故事之大者使相係銜。

translations.literal: Under the old rule, edicts issued from Zhongshu Menxia; for major precedents commissioner-ministers co-signed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule edicts came from the Secretariat; major precedents required commissioner-ministers to co-sign.

sentences.zh: 至是，皆南省奉行，而開府不預。

translations.literal: By then all were handled by the southern ministries, and the Palace Keeper did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Now the southern ministries handled everything, and the Palace Keeper no longer took part.

sentences.zh: 八年，鎮江軍節度使、檢校太傅韓絳為開府儀同三司、判大名府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Han Jiang, military commissioner of Zhenjiang Army and Acting Grand Mentor, was made Palace Keeper with Equal Ceremony and Adjudicator of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1085 Han Jiang, military commissioner of Zhenjiang Army and Acting Grand Mentor, became Palace Keeper with Equal Ceremony and was assigned to adjudicate Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年，太師、平章軍國重事文彥博為開府儀同三司、守太師、充護國軍山南西道節度使致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou, Grand Preceptor and Commissioner for Important State Affairs Wen Yanbo was made Palace Keeper with Equal Ceremony, retained Grand Preceptor, and was appointed retired military commissioner of Huguo Army on the Southwestern Shanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1090 Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo, who was directing state affairs, became Palace Keeper with Equal Ceremony, kept his grand preceptorship, and retired as military commissioner of Huguo Army on the Southwestern Shanxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 自崇寧五年司空、左僕射蔡京為開府儀同三司、安遠軍節度使、中太一宮使，其後故相而除則有劉正夫、餘深，前執政則有蔡攸、梁子美，外戚則有向宗回、宗良、鄭紳、錢景臻，殿帥則有高俅，內侍則有童貫、梁師成。

translations.literal: From the fifth year of Chongning, Minister of Works and Left Vice Director Cai Jing was made Palace Keeper with Equal Ceremony, military commissioner of Anyuan Army, and Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace; thereafter former chancellors so appointed included Liu Zhengfu and Yu Shen; former chief ministers included Cai You and Liang Zimei; affinal kin included Xiang Zonghui, Zongliang, Zheng Shen, and Qian Jingzhen; the palace commander was Gao Qiu; eunuchs included Tong Guan and Liang Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: From 1106 Cai Jing, Minister of Works and Left Vice Director, received Palace Keeper with Equal Ceremony, the Anyuan military commission, and the Central Grand Unity Palace; later former chancellors Liu Zhengfu and Yu Shen, former chief ministers Cai You and Liang Zimei, affinal kin Xiang Zonghui, Zongliang, Zheng Shen, and Qian Jingzhen, palace commander Gao Qiu, and eunuchs Tong Guan and Liang Shicheng were among those so honored.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，節度使至六十人，議者以為濫。

translations.literal: By late Xuanhe military commissioners reached sixty persons; critics deemed it excessive.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Xuanhe era there were sixty military commissioners, which critics called excessive.

sentences.zh: 〈（親王、皇子二十六人，宗室十一人，前執政二人，大將四人，外戚十人，宦者恩澤計七人。）〉）

translations.literal: (Twenty-six imperial princes and sons of the emperor, eleven clansmen, two former chief ministers, four great generals, ten affinal kin, and seven eunuchs favored by grace.)
translations.idiomatic: (Twenty-six imperial princes and imperial sons, eleven clansmen, two former chief ministers, four great generals, ten affinal relatives, and seven eunuchs favored by grace.)

sentences.zh: 中興，諸州升改節鎭凡十有二。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, twelve prefectures in all were elevated or converted to military commission capitals.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration twelve prefectures were elevated or converted into military commission capitals.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸將勳名有兼兩鎭、三鎭者，實爲希闊之典。

translations.literal: At that time generals of merit might hold two or three commissions—truly a rare precedent.
translations.idiomatic: By then celebrated generals might hold two or even three military commissions—a truly rare honor.

sentences.zh: （宋朝元臣拜兩鎭節度使者才三人：韓琦、文彦博、中興後呂頤浩是也。

translations.literal: (Only three great ministers of the Song received two military commissions: Han Qi, Wen Yanbo, and after the Restoration Lu Yihau.
translations.idiomatic: (Only three Song great ministers ever held two military commissions: Han Qi, Wen Yanbo, and after the Restoration Lu Yihau.

sentences.zh: 三公卒辭之。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes always declined them.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes always declined the honor.

sentences.zh: 而諸大將若韓、張、呂、嶽、楊劉之流，率至兩鎮節度使，其後加至三鎮者三人：韓世忠鎮南、武安、寧國，張俊靜江、寧武、靜海，劉錡護國、寧武、保靜。）〉

translations.literal: But great generals such as Han, Zhang, Lü, Yue, and the Yang and Liu lines mostly reached two military commissions; later three were added for three men: Han Shizhong held Zhennan, Wu'an, and Ningguo; Zhang Jun held Jingjiang, Ningwu, and Jinghai; Liu Qi held Huguo, Ningwu, and Baojing.)
translations.idiomatic: Field commanders such as Han, Zhang, Lü, Yue, and the Yang and Liu families usually held two commissions; only three later held three—Han Shizhong (Zhennan, Wu'an, Ningguo), Zhang Jun (Jingjiang, Ningwu, Jinghai), and Liu Qi (Huguo, Ningwu, Baojing).)

sentences.zh: 其後相承，宰執從官及后妃之族拜者不一。

translations.literal: Thereafter the practice continued, and chief ministers, attendant officials, and consort kin were appointed in no small number.
translations.idiomatic: The practice continued, and many chief ministers, court attendants, and consort kin received the title.

sentences.zh: 然自建炎至嘉泰，宰相特拜者六人，呂頤浩、張浚、虞允文皆以勳，史浩以舊，趙雄、葛邲以恩。

translations.literal: Yet from Jianyan to Jiatai, only six chief ministers received special appointment: Lü Yihau, Zhang Jun, and Yu Yunwen for merit; Shi Hao for seniority; Zhao Xiong and Ge Tan for favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Jianyan to Jiatai only six chief ministers received it by special appointment: Lü Yihau, Zhang Jun, and Yu Yunwen for merit; Shi Hao for seniority; Zhao Xiong and Ge Tan for favor.

sentences.zh: 執政一人，

translations.literal: One chief minister,
translations.idiomatic: One chief minister,

sentences.zh: 〈（葉右丞夢得。）〉

translations.literal: (Right Vice Director Ye Mengde.)
translations.idiomatic: (Right Vice Director Ye Mengde.)

sentences.zh: 從官二人而已。

translations.literal: and only two attendant officials.
translations.idiomatic: and only two attendant officials.

sentences.zh: 〈（張端明澄、楊敷學倓。）〉

translations.literal: (Bright-Illumination Academician Zhang Cheng and Academician Yang Tan.)
translations.idiomatic: (Bright-Illumination Academician Zhang Cheng and Academician Yang Tan.)

sentences.zh: 惟紹興中曹勳、韓公裔，乾道中曾覿，嘉泰中薑特立、譙令雍，皆以攀附恩澤，亦累官至焉，非常制也。

translations.literal: Only in Shaoxing Cao Xun and Han Gongyi, in Qiandao Zeng Di, and in Jiatai Jiang Teli and Qiao Lingyong—by climbing to favor—also repeatedly reached it; this was not the regular rule.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Shaoxing Cao Xun and Han Gongyi, in Qiandao Zeng Di, and in Jiatai Jiang Teli and Qiao Lingyong—through court favor—also rose to the post repeatedly, outside the normal rule.

sentences.zh: 【承宣使】無定員，舊名節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: Commissioner of Promotion: no fixed quota; formerly called Military Observation Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Title: Commissioner of Promotion. There was no fixed quota; the old name was Military Observation Deputy.

sentences.zh: 政和七年，詔：「觀察留後乃五季藩鎮官以所親信留充後務之稱，不可循用，可冠以軍名，改為承宣使。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenghe, an edict said: "Military observation deputies were Five Dynasties frontier titles for trusted retainers left to manage rear affairs and must not be followed; they may be prefixed with an army name and changed to Commissioner of Promotion."
translations.idiomatic: In 1117 an edict declared: "The observation deputy was a Five Dynasties frontier title for a commander's trusted retainer left behind to manage rear affairs and must not be reused; prefix it with an army name and rename it Commissioner of Promotion."

sentences.zh: 唐有留後，五代因之，宋初，留後、觀察皆不得本州刺史。

translations.literal: Tang had deputies; the Five Dynasties continued them; in early Song deputies and observers could not hold the home prefecture's governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had such deputies; the Five Dynasties kept them; early in the Song, deputies and observers could not also serve as the home prefecture's governor.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，令有司檢討故事，始復帶之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an order had the relevant offices review precedents, and they were first allowed to hold it concurrently again.
translations.idiomatic: In 1014 the court ordered a review of precedents and again allowed concurrent appointment.

sentences.zh: 【觀察使】無定員。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Title: Observation Commissioner. There was no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 初沿唐制置諸州觀察使。

translations.literal: At first the Tang system of observation commissioners for various prefectures was followed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Tang practice of observation commissioners for various prefectures was followed.

sentences.zh: 凡諸衛將軍及使遙領者，資品並止本官敘，政和中，詔承宣、觀察使仍不帶持節等。

translations.literal: For all guard generals and commissioners holding titles in absentia, rank followed the base office; in Zhenghe an edict said commissioners of promotion and observation still did not carry credential tokens and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Guard generals and commissioners holding titles in absentia ranked by their base office; in Zhenghe an edict said commissioners of promotion and observation still did not carry credential tokens and the like.

sentences.zh: 【防禦使】團練使諸州刺史無定員。

translations.literal: Defense Commissioner and Training Commissioner: prefectural governors had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Title: Defense Commissioner and Training Commissioner. Prefectural governors had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，臣僚言：「遙郡、正任恩數遼絕，自遙郡適正任者，合次第轉行。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, officials memorialized: "Remote-hold and regular-hold favor privileges are vastly different; those moving from remote-hold to regular-hold should advance step by step.
translations.idiomatic: In 1126 officials memorialized: "Remote-hold and regular-hold titles differ greatly in privilege; promotion from remote-hold to regular-hold should proceed step by step.

sentences.zh: 今自遙郡與落階官而授正任，直超轉本等正官，是皆奸巧希進躐取。

translations.literal: Now from remote-hold and demoted-rank offices one is appointed directly to regular-hold at the full rank of the title—this is all crafty striving to leap ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Today men jump from remote-hold or demoted-rank posts straight to full regular-hold rank—an obvious trick to leapfrog promotion.

sentences.zh: 乞應遙郡承宣使有功勞除正任者，止除正任刺史。」

translations.literal: I beg that for remote-hold commissioners of promotion with merit appointed to regular-hold, they be limited to regular-hold prefect.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that a remote-hold commissioner of promotion promoted for merit receive only regular-hold prefect, not higher rank."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 凡未落階官者為遙郡，除落階官者為正任。

translations.literal: Those not yet stripped of demoted rank were remote-hold; those stripped of demoted rank were regular-hold.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone still carrying a demoted rank was remote-hold; once the demoted rank was removed he was regular-hold.

sentences.zh: 朝謁禦宴，惟正任預焉。

translations.literal: At court audience and imperial banquets, only regular-hold officers participated.
translations.idiomatic: Only regular-hold officers attended court audience and imperial banquets.

sentences.zh: 遙郡並止本官敘，正任復次第轉行，考之舊制，梯級有差。

translations.literal: Remote-hold titles ranked only by the base office; regular-hold advanced step by step—examining the old rule, the ladder of grades differed.
translations.idiomatic: Remote-hold titles ranked only by the base office, while regular-hold advanced in steps; under the old rules the ladder was clearly graded.

sentences.zh: 中興以後，節度移鎮浸少，後有一定不易徑遷太尉；

translations.literal: After the Restoration, transfers of military commissions grew rare, and later there was a fixed path that did not easily lead straight to Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration military commission transfers grew rare, and later a fixed path no longer led easily straight to Grand Marshal;

sentences.zh: 承宣、觀察徑作一官，及遙郡落階官久就除正任。

translations.literal: commissioners of promotion and observation were treated as a single rank, and remote-hold officers long stripped of demoted rank were soon given regular-hold.
translations.idiomatic: commissioners of promotion and observation were treated as one rank, and remote-hold officers who had long since shed demoted rank were quickly given regular-hold.

sentences.zh: 紹興末，臣僚以為言，雖復置檢校官，餘未盡改。

translations.literal: In late Shaoxing, officials spoke on this; although acting titles were restored, the rest was not fully changed.
translations.idiomatic: In late Shaoxing officials raised the issue; although acting titles were restored, the other abuses were not fully corrected.
